{"parentUuid":"a8d49bdc-b59d-4be5-9a1c-1e04ae3419c6","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"6b9fc511-f186-4a71-8368-e982a48fe928","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_011HNxYJ7NgUBuYnHFKt7u2m","type":"tool_result","content":"=== CONTEXT-FORMAT ===\n# CONTEXT.md Format\n\n## Structure\n\n```md\n# {Context Name}\n\n{One or two sentence description of what this context is and why it exists.}\n\n## Language\n\n**Order**:\n{A one or two sentence description of the term}\n_Avoid_: Purchase, transaction\n\n**Invoice**:\nA request for payment sent to a customer after delivery.\n_Avoid_: Bill, payment request\n\n**Customer**:\nA person or organization that places orders.\n_Avoid_: Client, buyer, account\n```\n\n## Rules\n\n- **Be opinionated.** When multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the others under `_Avoid_`.\n- **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences max. Define what it IS, not what it does.\n- **Only include terms specific to this project's context.** General programming concepts (timeouts, error types, utility patterns) don't belong even if the project uses them extensively. Before adding a term, ask: is this a concept unique to this context, or a general programming concept? Only the former belongs.\n- **Group terms under subheadings** when natural clusters emerge. If all terms belong to a single cohesive area, a flat list is fine.\n\n## Single vs multi-context repos\n\n**Single context (most repos):** One `CONTEXT.md` at the repo root.\n\n**Multiple contexts:** A `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the repo root lists the contexts, where they live, and how they relate to each other:\n\n```md\n# Context Map\n\n## Contexts\n\n- [Ordering](./src/ordering/CONTEXT.md): receives and tracks customer orders\n- [Billing](./src/billing/CONTEXT.md): generates invoices and processes payments\n- [Fulfillment](./src/fulfillment/CONTEXT.md): manages warehouse picking and shipping\n\n## Relationships\n\n- **Ordering → Fulfillment**: Ordering emits `OrderPlaced` events; Fulfillment consumes them to start picking\n- **Fulfillment → Billing**: Fulfillment emits `ShipmentDispatched` events; Billing consumes them to generate invoices\n- **Ordering ↔ Billing**: Shared types for `CustomerId` and `Money`\n```\n\nThe skill infers which structure applies:\n\n- If `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists, read it to find contexts\n- If only a root `CONTEXT.md` exists, single context\n- If neither exists, create a root `CONTEXT.md` lazily when the first term is resolved\n\nWhen multiple contexts exist, infer which one the current topic relates to. If unclear, ask.\n=== ADR-FORMAT ===\n# ADR Format\n\nADRs live in `docs/adr/` and use sequential numbering: `0001-slug.md`, `0002-slug.md`, etc.\n\nCreate the `docs/adr/` directory lazily: only when the first ADR is needed.\n\n## Template\n\n```md\n# {Short title of the decision}\n\n{1-3 sentences: what's the context, what did we decide, and why.}\n```\n\nThat's it. An ADR can be a single paragraph. The value is in recording *that* a decision was made and *why*, not in filling out sections.\n\n## Optional sections\n\nOnly include these when they add genuine value. Most ADRs won't need them.\n\n- **Status** frontmatter (`proposed | accepted | deprecated | superseded by ADR-NNNN`): useful when decisions are revisited\n- **Considered Options**: only when the rejected alternatives are worth remembering\n- **Consequences**: only when non-obvious downstream effects need to be called out\n\n## Numbering\n\nScan `docs/adr/` for the highest existing number and increment by one.\n\n## When to offer an ADR\n\nAll three of these must be true:\n\n1. **Hard to reverse**: the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful\n2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will look at the code and wonder \"why on earth did they do it this way?\"\n3. **The result of a real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons\n\nIf a decision is easy to reverse, skip it: you'll just reverse it. If it's not surprising, nobody will wonder why. If there was no real alternative, there's nothing to record beyond \"we did the obvious thing.\"\n\n### What qualifies\n\n- **Architectural shape.** \"We're using a monorepo.\" \"The write model is event-sourced, the read model is projected into Postgres.\"\n- **Integration patterns between contexts.** \"Ordering and Billing communicate via domain events, not synchronous HTTP.\"\n- **Technology choices that carry lock-in.** Database, message bus, auth provider, deployment target. Not every library: just the ones that would take a quarter to swap out.\n- **Boundary and scope decisions.** \"Customer data is owned by the Customer context; other contexts reference it by ID only.\" The explicit no-s are as valuable as the yes-s.\n- **Deliberate deviations from the obvious path.** \"We're using manual SQL instead of an ORM because X.\" Anything where a reasonable reader would assume the opposite. These stop the next engineer from \"fixing\" something that was deliberate.\n- **Constraints not visible in the code.** \"We can't use AWS because of compliance requirements.\" \"Response times must be under 200ms because of the partner API contract.\"\n- **Rejected alternatives when the rejection is non-obvious.** If you considered GraphQL and picked REST for subtle reasons, record it; otherwise someone will suggest GraphQL again in six months.\n=== existing ADRs ===\nADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md\nADR-002-stack.md","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"e52c4197-ddab-4b38-b5a8-a1112ce68a5d","timestamp":"2026-10-04T22:28:06.372Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"=== CONTEXT-FORMAT ===\n# CONTEXT.md Format\n\n## Structure\n\n```md\n# {Context Name}\n\n{One or two sentence description of what this context is and why it exists.}\n\n## Language\n\n**Order**:\n{A one or two sentence description of the term}\n_Avoid_: Purchase, transaction\n\n**Invoice**:\nA request for payment sent to a customer after delivery.\n_Avoid_: Bill, payment request\n\n**Customer**:\nA person or organization that places orders.\n_Avoid_: Client, buyer, account\n```\n\n## Rules\n\n- **Be opinionated.** When multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the others under `_Avoid_`.\n- **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences max. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.\n\nFormat a round like so:\n\n```\n❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>\n\n➡️ <your recommended answer>\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q2** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>\n\n➡️ <your recommended answer>\n```\n\nEach round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.\n\nFinding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it; don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's: put each to them and wait.\n\nThe session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. {"parentUuid":"90963803-ab7f-4286-9004-22a9bf5ec063","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"6b9fc511-f186-4a71-8368-e982a48fe928","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/adam_leider/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/domain-modeling\n\n# Domain Modeling\n\nActively build and sharpen the project's domain model as you design. This is the *active* discipline: challenging terms, inventing edge-case scenarios, and writing the glossary and decisions down the moment they crystallise. (Merely *reading* `CONTEXT.md` for vocabulary is not this skill: that's a one-line habit any skill can do. This skill is for when you're changing the model, not just consuming it.)\n\n## File structure\n\nMost repos have a single context:\n\n```\n/\n├── CONTEXT.md\n├── docs/\n│   └── adr/\n│       ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md\n│       └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md\n└── src/\n```\n\nIf a `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists at the root, the repo has multiple contexts. The map points to where each one lives:\n\n```\n/\n├── CONTEXT-MAP.md\n├── docs/\n│   └── adr/                          ← system-wide decisions\n├── src/\n│   ├── ordering/\n│   │   ├── CONTEXT.md\n│   │   └── docs/adr/                 ← context-specific decisions\n│   └── billing/\n│       ├── CONTEXT.md\n│       └── docs/adr/\n```\n\nCreate files lazily: only when you have something to write. If no `CONTEXT.md` exists, create one when the first term is resolved. If no `docs/adr/` exists, create it when the first ADR is needed.\n\n## During the session\n\n### Challenge against the glossary\n\nWhen the user uses a term that conflicts with the existing language in `CONTEXT.md`, call it out immediately. \"Your glossary defines 'cancellation' as X, but you seem to mean Y. Which is it?\"\n\n### Sharpen fuzzy language\n\nWhen the user uses vague or overloaded terms, propose a precise canonical term. \"You're saying 'account': do you mean the Customer or the User? Those are different things.\"\n\n### Discuss concrete scenarios\n\nWhen domain relationships are being discussed, stress-test them with specific scenarios. Invent scenarios that probe edge cases and force the user to be precise about the boundaries between concepts.\n\n### Cross-reference with code\n\nWhen the user states how something works, check whether the code agrees. If you find a contradiction, surface it: \"Your code cancels entire Orders, but you just said partial cancellation is possible. Which is right?\"\n\n### Update CONTEXT.md inline\n\nWhen a term is resolved, update `CONTEXT.md` right there. Don't batch these up: capture them as they happen. Use the format in [CONTEXT-FORMAT.md](./CONTEXT-FORMAT.md).\n\n`CONTEXT.md` should be totally devoid of implementation details. Do not treat `CONTEXT.md` as a spec, a scratch pad, or a repository for implementation decisions. It is a glossary and nothing else.\n\n### Offer ADRs sparingly\n\nOnly offer to create an ADR when all three are true:\n\n1. **Hard to reverse**: the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful\n2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will wonder \"why did they do it this way?\"\n3. **The result of a real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons\n\nIf any of the three is missing, skip the ADR. Use the format in [ADR-FORMAT.md](./ADR-FORMAT.md).\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Repo is single-context: CONTEXT.md at root is currently just a stub, docs/adr/ already has ADR-001 and ADR-002 (numbered ADR-00N-slug.md, not the 0001- default). Update CONTEXT.md inline as terms settle during the grill; only offer an ADR for boundary/trade-off decisions that are hard to reverse and would surprise a future reader (e.g. the no-live-server exclusions)."}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"89495c89-b1ad-4a4a-8e49-ffc1e819c128","timestamp":"2026-10-04T22:29:18.956Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_017hHZRQEPQMZvfktp4GCFtq","session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"be1a2e02-a7bd-457b-886b-2f47f7221c4e","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfhzCf4h7pNXoRxc9kWTZ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Both skills are loaded — `grilling` for the interview, `domain-modeling` to capture terms into `CONTEXT.md`/ADRs as they settle. (The wrapper `/grill-with-docs` itself can't be invoked through the Skill tool — it's explicitly reserved for the harness's own slash-command handling — but its whole job was just dispatching those two, which are now running.)\n\nI've read the manual's §3.3 (the 7 fixed capabilities), your field notes, and the client brief. `CONTEXT.md` is still a stub and `docs/adr/` has ADR-001 and ADR-002, so I'll number new ones `ADR-003` onward to match.\n\nNothing is settled yet, so no glossary edits this round — here's the frontier:\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q1** - **Content hierarchy: are continent/country pages real content, or generated listings?**: The brief wants Home → Continent → Country → Program → Posts. Capability 4 only requires one flat \"Pages\" type that shows in nav. Two ways to get the brief's hierarchy out of that:\n\n(a) Continent, Country, and Program are all **Pages**, linked by a `parent_id`, each with its own slug and an editable Markdown body — CGE could write \"Studying in Spain\" copy on the Spain page itself.\n(b) Only **Program** is a real Page. Continent and Country are **generated index views** (built at `cms publish` time by grouping Programs by their `continent`/`country` fields) — nobody authors them directly, they just list the Programs/children under them.\n\n(a) costs more admin surface (4 levels of CRUD) but matches \"organized into continent pages\" literally and lets CGE add context at each level. (b) is cheaper and still satisfies capability 4, but a continent page is just a directory listing with no body text.\n\n➡️ (a) — your brief twice says \"continent pages\" and \"country pages\" as things, not just groupings, and CGE sounds like they'll want to write a line or two of orientation copy at each level (\"Why Kenyon partners in East Asia,\" etc.).\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q2** - **\"Hot topic\" sections — a Post field, or a second content type?**: Each Program has \"general blog posts, as well as a couple of sections relating to hot topics\" (housing, meals, social life, academics…). Is \"hot topic\" just a **category field on Post** (e.g. `topic: general | housing | meals | social-life | academics | other`), or does a hot-topic section need to be its own content type (closer to a Page) that then *contains* posts?\n\n➡️ A category field on Post. The manual fixes exactly two content types (Posts, Pages) as the required capabilities — inventing a third (\"Section\") to hold topic-grouped posts isn't one of the 7 and isn't asked for by the brief, which describes topics as something posts are \"tailored towards,\" i.e. a property of the post, not a container.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q3** - **Role naming: is the admin/editor split strictly CGE-staff vs. ambassador, 1:1?**: The manual fixes two roles. Your brief says CGE staff have \"full administrative privileges\" and ambassadors can \"write blog posts but not edit the site further than that.\" Before I write this into `CONTEXT.md` as `admin = CGE staff`, `editor = student ambassador`: could a CGE staff member ever hold the *editor* (ambassador-level) account instead of admin — e.g., a part-time staffer who should only write, not manage users? Or is \"CGE staff\" always admin, full stop, and \"editor\" always means \"ambassador,\" full stop?\n\n➡️ Strict 1:1 as your brief implies (CGE staff = admin, ambassador = editor), with no mixed case. If a future staffer needs write-only access, that's still just \"give them the editor role\" — the role is about *permissions*, not *job title*, so the system doesn't need to know someone is \"staff\" vs. \"ambassador,\" only \"admin\" vs. \"editor.\" I'd record the role names in `CONTEXT.md` as `admin`/`editor` (the manual's terms) with `CGE staff`/`student ambassador` noted as the client-facing labels to avoid, per rule 2 of the workflow (\"call it a bulletin and the model calls it a post... two designs\").\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q4** - **Review workflow: what can an ambassador do to a post after CGE reviews it?**: Your hard constraint is \"never publish without review, never touch anyone else's post, nothing unapproved goes public.\" Mapping that onto capability 3's draft/published status: ambassador can create/edit/delete their **own** posts while `status = draft`; only admin can flip `draft → published`. Open question: once published, can the ambassador who wrote it still edit it (e.g., fix a typo), or does editing it require an admin to unpublish it back to draft first?\n\n➡️ Ambassador loses edit/delete rights on their own post the moment it's published — any further change (typo fix included) means admin unpublishes it back to draft, ambassador edits, admin re-publishes. This is the simplest reading of \"never publish without review\" (a silent post-publish edit is an unreviewed change) and needs no third status beyond the two the manual already fixes.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q5** - **Scope boundary: confirm the brief's \"add next\" wishlist is out of MP2's scope**: Private messaging, visitor/comment accounts, an IT/dev role, and view/comment-based search filters are all in your brief's own \"What I'd add next\" section, and two of the four are explicitly flagged there as needing \"a live server\" — which conflicts with the manual's architecture (admin console laptop-only, public site static HTML, Part 0.2). Confirm these four are **out of scope** for MP2 and get recorded as a boundary decision (likely ADR-003), not silently dropped?\n\n➡️ Yes, out of scope — and worth an ADR, because it's hard to reverse (adding a live server later is a real architectural shift, not a tweak), surprising without context (a reader sees the brief's wishlist and wonders why none of it got built), and a genuine trade-off (static-publish simplicity and the laptop-only security story vs. these features).\n\n---\n\nOne more, lower in the tree but askable now since it doesn't depend on the above:\n\n❓ **Q6** - **Search: is the brief's search function (countries/programs/posts, filtered by date/relevance) in scope at all?**: It's not one of the 7 required capabilities, but unlike Q5's wishlist items it's in the brief's main body, not \"add next,\" and doesn't need a live server — it could run as a client-side search over a JSON index built at publish time. Build it as an extra (8th) feature, or treat it as out of scope for MP2 and revisit after the 7 required capabilities ship?\n\n➡️ Out of scope for MP2. The manual's time budget (11–14 hrs for exactly 7 capabilities) and its own \"deliberately excluded\" framing argue against adding an 8th feature not on the fixed list, even a feasible one — ship the 7 first; a static JSON-index search is a clean follow-up ticket afterward, not a day-one requirement."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":8766,"cache_read_input_tokens":62672,"output_tokens":5422,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":3069},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":8766,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":5422,"cache_read_input_tokens":62672,"cache_creation_input_tokens":8766,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":8766},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CfhzCejr5Bxjsmoo2hd25","attributionSkill":"mattpocock-skills:domain-modeling","attributionPlugin":"mattpocock-skills","type":"assistant","uuid":"471e2f85-0501-4f10-a5ee-be3c68fd07cc","timestamp":"2026-10-04T22:30:26.125Z","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"5924dfb0-206d-4e20-9b0c-62a65bb69cbc","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"6c7865ed-c5db-4b94-a2ab-0a67d5344d3c","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"A1: Each level is its own page linked by a parent. This build is a demo. Seed Asia, Africa, and Europe in the homepage, add a couple countries under each, with one or two sample programs under each of the countries. Each should have placeholder text that you generate, that makes sense for the page. The homepage can have some information about what the website is and its goal, as well as the links to those continents. Each will have information that makes sense about them, and same for the countries. Just create basic and sensible sounding fictional study-abroad programs to put in the country sections. This information will be created by seed_demo.py. CGE admins can add more continents, countries, and programs later through the normal page editor. No special template features, they're just regular pages. \nA2: Yes, hot topic is a category field on Post, with the options you listed. Program pages show the posts grouped by topic, a bit like forum sections: students click a topic like Housing to see just those posts. Read-only, though; no replies or discussion, since the public site is static.\nA3: A CGE staff member should be able to write posts as well if they desire; they should have all the tools the ambassador role has. The role names shown in the site and CONTEXT.md can be Staff and Ambassador, but in the code they stay admin (Staff) and editor (Ambassador).\nA4 : Ambassadors write drafts, then submit them for review, which sets the post to pending. They can edit their own post while it's in a draft, but not once it's pending or published. CGE admins approve pending posts by publishing them, or send them back to draft. If an ambassador wants a change after that, they contact CGE outside the site. Built in suggested edits are a nice idea but out of scope for this build. \nA5: Yes, all four are out of scope and worth an ADR. Add \"suggested edits\" from my last answer to the same list. CGE could live without these at launch, since students can already email CGE or ambassadors directly, which covers most of what messaging would do. \nA6: Search matters to CGE, but scoped per page: on a continent page it searches only that continent's countries, programs and posts; on a country page, only that country; on a program page, only that program's posts. Program pages should also let students filter posts by topic (General or a hot topic). The topic filter is part of the core build. The scoped search is a stretch ticket, built client-side from a JSON index made at publish time, if time allows after the 7 capabilities."},"uuid":"42c2719f-2f0f-4fd9-9c70-361a222aaaa0","timestamp":"2026-10-05T03:31:49.404Z","permissionMode":"bypassPermissions","origin":{"kind":"human"},"promptSource":"typed","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

A local admin console\n(FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite) writes content; `cms publish` renders the published\ncontent into `site/` as static HTML, which is deployed to GitHub Pages. The\nadmin console never goes on the public internet.\n\n## Hard constraints\n\n- Published HTML uses **relative** paths only. Never `href=\"/...\"` or `src=\"/...\"`.\n- Never commit `.env`, `*.db`, keys, or tokens. Read secrets from the environment.\n- Passwords are hashed with argon2. Never store or log a plain password.\n- Every state-changing form carries a CSRF token.\n- User-written Markdown is sanitized before it is rendered anywhere.\n- `site/` is generated. Never edit it by hand.\n- Only published content reaches `site/`. Drafts never leave the database.\n\n## How to work with me\n\n- One ticket per session. {"parentUuid":"76ee7d63-d091-4a80-87a1-58a2265fec98","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"6c7865ed-c5db-4b94-a2ab-0a67d5344d3c","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01EXTGdzTTuU8qE1CEyZVkJ8","type":"tool_result","content":"=== ADR-001 ===\n# ADR-001: The admin console runs locally; the public site is a static export\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nA CMS needs a server, a database, and login. GitHub Pages serves static files\nonly: it cannot run Python and has no database. Students have two weeks and no\nhosting budget, and a first web application with real authentication is an\nattractive target the moment it is public.\n\n## Decision\n\nThe admin console (FastAPI + SQLite) runs on the student's own machine. A\n`cms publish` step renders the published content to static HTML in `site/`, which\nis deployed to GitHub Pages on the `gh-pages` branch.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Login, roles, and the database are never exposed to the internet.\n- The public site cannot have server-side features (search, comments) without a\n  different host; a stretch goal may add a live admin deploy behind a security gate.\n- Publishing is explicit: content changes are not live until `cms publish` runs,\n  which is a behaviour worth documenting for your client.\n- Relative paths become mandatory, because Pages serves the site from a subfolder.\n\n## Why this is an ADR\n\nIt is hard to reverse (it shapes every route, template, and deploy step) and it\nis surprising without context (most CMSes are servers). That is the bar; most\ndecisions do not meet it and belong in the spec or the glossary instead.\n\n=== ADR-002 ===\n# ADR-002: FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, with no frontend framework\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nThe project has to be readable by someone who has never built a web application,\ngradable from a clean clone, and finishable in two weeks on a $20 plan. Options\nconsidered: Django (batteries included, but a large amount of generated code to\nread), Flask (similar to FastAPI here), a JavaScript stack (a second language and\na build step), and FastAPI with server-rendered templates.\n\n## Decision\n\nFastAPI with Jinja2 templates, SQLite for storage, argon2 for password hashing,\nand an HTML sanitizer for user Markdown. No frontend framework, no build step.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Every page is server-rendered, so \"view source\" shows what the code produced,\n  which makes debugging visible.\n- SQLite is a single file, so a grader can seed and inspect it easily. It is\n  gitignored; `scripts/seed_demo.py` rebuilds it.\n- No build step means the file you preview is the file that ships.\n- Interactive flourishes (live preview without reload, drag-and-drop) cost more\n  here than in a JavaScript stack. That is an accepted trade.\n\n=== client-brief ===\n# Client brief: Kenyon Center for Global Engagement\n\nThis site should be run by the Kenyon Center for Global Engagement. They are fairly comfortable with computers but it should be relatively easy and intuitive to navigate.\n\nThe people reading the site are Kenyon students (or students from other universities) looking for information on different study abroad programs. They want to read blog posts on the experience, as well as specific posts tailored towards questions about housing, meal plans, social life, academics, and other hot topics.\n...\n=== field-notes exists? ===\nnotes/client-brief.md\nnotes/cms-field-notes.md\nnotes/setup_check.md\nnotes/token-budget-plan.md","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"ab43d536-46e7-4a01-a818-1b9a1dfd43f3","timestamp":"2026-10-05T03:33:11.481Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"=== ADR-001 ===\n# ADR-001: The admin console runs locally; the public site is a static export\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nA CMS needs a server, a database, and login. {"parentUuid":"8b80b6f4-d55e-4df6-8099-14e9484accfb","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfiPUqjktv1MYtCKZxCiT","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01U5ueXLhKicv2vvHNCCXDuA","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400/CONTEXT.md","content":"# Kenyon CGE Study Abroad CMS\n\nGlossary for the CMS built for the Kenyon Center for Global Engagement's study\nabroad blog. Client: `notes/client-brief.md`. The 7 fixed capabilities this\nvocabulary has to satisfy: `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` §3.3.\n\n## Language\n\n**Page**:\nSite content that sits in a fixed tree — Home, then Continent, then Country,\nthen Program — and appears in the public navigation once published. Rendering\nis uniform across every level: a Page lists its child Pages if it has any, and\nits own Posts grouped by Topic if it has any. There is no separate template per\nlevel. Staff add more Continents, Countries, and Programs later through the\nnormal page editor, the same way the seed set was created.\n_Avoid_: continent page, country page, program page as if they were distinct\ntypes — they are all just Pages at different places in the tree.\n\n**Post**:\nA dated blog entry written under a Program Page: title, slug, Markdown body,\nTopic, author, timestamps, and a status of draft, pending, or published.\n_Avoid_: entry, article.\n\n**Topic**:\nThe category a Post is tagged with, used to group and filter Posts on their\nProgram page like forum sections (read-only — no replies or discussion):\nGeneral, Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics, or Other.\n_Avoid_: \"hot topic\" as a separate concept from Topic — General is just one\nTopic value among the others, not a different kind of thing.\n\n**Status** (of a Post):\ndraft → pending → published. *Draft*: the author is still writing; only they\ncan edit it, and it is not public. *Pending*: the author has submitted it for\nreview and can no longer edit it; it is still not public. *Published*: CGE has\napproved it and it is live on the public site. Only an admin can move a Post\ninto or out of published, and only an admin can bounce pending back to draft.\n_Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list\nnames only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit\nsubmit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004).\n\n**Role**:\nTwo roles, per the manual: *admin*, shown in the UI as **Staff**, and *editor*,\nshown in the UI as **Ambassador**. The mapping is strict and permission-based,\nnot title-based — admin/editor stay the internal/code names (the manual's own\nvocabulary); Staff/Ambassador are what the site and this glossary call them.\nStaff have every capability Ambassadors have (they can write and submit Posts\ntoo) plus admin-only capabilities (publish, user management).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\" / \"student ambassador\" in place of Staff/Ambassador once\ninside the CMS's own vocabulary — those are brief language, not the product's.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":6771,"cache_read_input_tokens":87961,"output_tokens":1061,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":6771,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1061,"cache_read_input_tokens":87961,"cache_creation_input_tokens":6771,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":6771},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01U5ueXLhKicv2vvHNCCXDuA":{"file_path":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400/CONTEXT.md","content":"# Kenyon CGE Study Abroad CMS\n\nGlossary for the CMS built for the Kenyon Center for Global Engagement's study\nabroad blog. Client: `notes/client-brief.md`. The 7 fixed capabilities this\nvocabulary has to satisfy: `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` §3.3.\n\n## Language\n\n**Page**:\nSite content that sits in a fixed tree — Home, then Continent, then Country,\nthen Program — and appears in the public navigation once published. Rendering\nis uniform across every level: a Page lists its child Pages if it has any, and\nits own Posts grouped by Topic if it has any. There is no separate template per\nlevel. Staff add more Continents, Countries, and Programs later through the\nnormal page editor, the same way the seed set was created.\n_Avoid_: continent page, country page, program page as if they were distinct\ntypes — they are all just Pages at different places in the tree.\n\n**Post**:\nA dated blog entry written under a Program Page: title, slug, Markdown body,\nTopic, author, timestamps, and a status of draft, pending, or published.\n_Avoid_: entry, article.\n\n**Topic**:\nThe category a Post is tagged with, used to group and filter Posts on their\nProgram page like forum sections (read-only — no replies or discussion):\nGeneral, Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics, or Other.\n_Avoid_: \"hot topic\" as a separate concept from Topic — General is just one\nTopic value among the others, not a different kind of thing.\n\n**Status** (of a Post):\ndraft → pending → published. *Draft*: the author is still writing; only they\ncan edit it, and it is not public. *Pending*: the author has submitted it for\nreview and can no longer edit it; it is still not public. *Published*: CGE has\napproved it and it is live on the public site. Only an admin can move a Post\ninto or out of published, and only an admin can bounce pending back to draft.\n_Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list\nnames only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit\nsubmit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004).\n\n**Role**:\nTwo roles, per the manual: *admin*, shown in the UI as **Staff**, and *editor*,\nshown in the UI as **Ambassador**. The mapping is strict and permission-based,\nnot title-based — admin/editor stay the internal/code names (the manual's own\nvocabulary); Staff/Ambassador are what the site and this glossary call them.\nStaff have every capability Ambassadors have (they can write and submit Posts\ntoo) plus admin-only capabilities (publish, user management).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\" / \"student ambassador\" in place of Staff/Ambassador once\ninside the CMS's own vocabulary — those are brief language, not the product's.\n"}},"apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CfiPUq2r1PXTX9DaGTNab","type":"assistant","uuid":"b7133952-addd-4faa-937c-bb64d5210137","timestamp":"2026-10-05T03:34:47.565Z","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

The 7 fixed capabilities this\nvocabulary has to satisfy: `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` §3.3.\n\n## Language\n\n**Page**:\nSite content that sits in a fixed tree — Home, then Continent, then Country,\nthen Program — and appears in the public navigation once published. Rendering\nis uniform across every level: a Page lists its child Pages if it has any, and\nits own Posts grouped by Topic if it has any. There is no separate template per\nlevel. Staff add more Continents, Countries, and Programs later through the\nnormal page editor, the same way the seed set was created.\n_Avoid_: continent page, country page, program page as if they were distinct\ntypes — they are all just Pages at different places in the tree.\n\n**Post**:\nA dated blog entry written under a Program Page: title, slug, Markdown body,\nTopic, author, timestamps, and a status of draft, pending, or published.\n_Avoid_: entry, article.\n\n**Topic**:\nThe category a Post is tagged with, used to group and filter Posts on their\nProgram page like forum sections (read-only — no replies or discussion):\nGeneral, Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics, or Other.\n_Avoid_: \"hot topic\" as a separate concept from Topic — General is just one\nTopic value among the others, not a different kind of thing.\n\n**Status** (of a Post):\ndraft → pending → published. *Draft*: the author is still writing; only they\ncan edit it, and it is not public. *Pending*: the author has submitted it for\nreview and can no longer edit it; it is still not public. *Published*: CGE has\napproved it and it is live on the public site. Only an admin can move a Post\ninto or out of published, and only an admin can bounce pending back to draft.\n_Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list\nnames only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit\nsubmit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004).\n\n**Role**:\nTwo roles, per the manual: *admin*, shown in the UI as **Staff**, and *editor*,\nshown in the UI as **Ambassador**. The mapping is strict and permission-based,\nnot title-based — admin/editor stay the internal/code names (the manual's own\nvocabulary); Staff/Ambassador are what the site and this glossary call them.\nStaff have every capability Ambassadors have (they can write and submit Posts\ntoo) plus admin-only capabilities (publish, user management).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\" / \"student ambassador\" in place of Staff/Ambassador once\ninside the CMS's own vocabulary — those are brief language, not the product's.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":3,"newStart":1,"newLines":49,"lines":["-# CONTEXT.md glossary","+# Kenyon CGE Study Abroad CMS"," ","-(Your /grill-with-docs session fills this in as terms are settled.)","+Glossary for the CMS built for the Kenyon Center for Global Engagement's study","+abroad blog. {"parentUuid":"f46a4aa2-b384-4f84-aaa9-1d1dbaf2307d","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"total_tokens_reminder","text":"<total_tokens>14981067 tokens left</total_tokens>"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"b99adb7f-b6e4-4edf-b1b8-acfbce91bd73","timestamp":"2026-10-05T03:34:47.710Z","rendered":[{"content":"<system-reminder>\n<total_tokens>14981067 tokens left</total_tokens>\n</system-reminder>"}],"session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}
{"parentUuid":"b99adb7f-b6e4-4edf-b1b8-acfbce91bd73","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfiPVnkTFxNmyhXa8yKBz","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01XRX7Kq3pFEis57AedE2fdA","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400/docs/adr/ADR-003-scope-exclusions-no-live-server.md","content":"# ADR-003: Messaging, visitor accounts, an IT role, usage-based filters, and suggested edits are out of scope\n\n**Status:** accepted\n**Date:** 2026-10-04\n\n## Context\n\nThe client brief's \"What I'd add next\" section lists private messaging, a\nvisitor/commenter account role, an IT/developer role, and search filters based\non view/comment counts — and says outright that messaging and the usage\nfilters \"need a live server.\" ADR-001 already fixed the admin console as\nlocal-only and the public site as a static export. Separately, while settling\nthe review workflow (ADR-004), built-in \"suggested edits\" — a way for an admin\nto leave an inline revision request on a bounced Post rather than talking to\nthe ambassador outside the CMS — came up and was rejected for the same reason:\nit is more review tooling than this build needs.\n\n## Decision\n\nNone of these five ship in this build: private messaging, a visitor/commenter\nrole, an IT/developer role, view/comment-based search filters, and in-CMS\nsuggested-edit tooling. When CGE bounces a pending Post back to draft, or a\nstudent wants to ask a follow-up question, that happens outside the CMS\n(email, in person) — the same channels that already exist today.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Students keep reaching ambassadors and CGE the way they already do; the\n  brief itself says this \"covers most of what messaging would do.\"\n- The review loop stays simple: bouncing pending → draft stores no reason and\n  starts no thread anywhere in the data model.\n- Revisiting messaging or usage-based counters later is an architecture\n  change (a live server), not a feature add — budget for it as the former.\n\n## Why this is an ADR\n\nHard to reverse: adding a live server later reopens ADR-001's whole\nlocal-admin/static-public shape. Surprising without context: the brief itself\nasks for these, so a reader needs to know they were deliberately deferred, not\nmissed. Genuine trade-off: static-site simplicity and the laptop-only security\nstory, against functionality the client explicitly wants eventually.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1184,"cache_read_input_tokens":94732,"output_tokens":808,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1184,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":808,"cache_read_input_tokens":94732,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1184,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1184},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01XRX7Kq3pFEis57AedE2fdA":{"file_path":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400/docs/adr/ADR-003-scope-exclusions-no-live-server.md","content":"# ADR-003: Messaging, visitor accounts, an IT role, usage-based filters, and suggested edits are out of scope\n\n**Status:** accepted\n**Date:** 2026-10-04\n\n## Context\n\nThe client brief's \"What I'd add next\" section lists private messaging, a\nvisitor/commenter account role, an IT/developer role, and search filters based\non view/comment counts — and says outright that messaging and the usage\nfilters \"need a live server.\" ADR-001 already fixed the admin console as\nlocal-only and the public site as a static export. Separately, while settling\nthe review workflow (ADR-004), built-in \"suggested edits\" — a way for an admin\nto leave an inline revision request on a bounced Post rather than talking to\nthe ambassador outside the CMS — came up and was rejected for the same reason:\nit is more review tooling than this build needs.\n\n## Decision\n\nNone of these five ship in this build: private messaging, a visitor/commenter\nrole, an IT/developer role, view/comment-based search filters, and in-CMS\nsuggested-edit tooling. When CGE bounces a pending Post back to draft, or a\nstudent wants to ask a follow-up question, that happens outside the CMS\n(email, in person) — the same channels that already exist today.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Students keep reaching ambassadors and CGE the way they already do; the\n  brief itself says this \"covers most of what messaging would do.\"\n- The review loop stays simple: bouncing pending → draft stores no reason and\n  starts no thread anywhere in the data model.\n- Revisiting messaging or usage-based counters later is an architecture\n  change (a live server), not a feature add — budget for it as the former.\n\n## Why this is an ADR\n\nHard to reverse: adding a live server later reopens ADR-001's whole\nlocal-admin/static-public shape. Surprising without context: the brief itself\nasks for these, so a reader needs to know they were deliberately deferred, not\nmissed. Genuine trade-off: static-site simplicity and the laptop-only security\nstory, against functionality the client explicitly wants eventually.\n"}},"apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CfiPVnVL1CEsbfXuDAcJG","type":"assistant","uuid":"8c1045ba-797b-4714-97d7-7dfc7f12ee7e","timestamp":"2026-10-05T03:34:57.201Z","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

{"parentUuid":"997ff07c-eaf8-4b2b-8931-52ffe181d227","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfiPWVwC1CuEzXDGgGG1d","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_016yJ7kKvSLcY9dZuwRD589L","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400/docs/adr/ADR-004-post-pending-status.md","content":"# ADR-004: Posts get a third status, pending, between draft and published\n\n**Status:** accepted\n**Date:** 2026-10-04\n\n## Context\n\nThe manual's capability 3 names only draft/published for Posts. The client's\nhard constraint — an ambassador must never publish without CGE review — can\nbe met with just those two states if \"draft\" simply means \"admin hasn't\npromoted this yet\" and the ambassador never controls a publish action. But\nthe client specifically wants an explicit submit-for-review step: an\nambassador finishes writing, hands it off, and loses edit access the moment\nthey do, before any admin has looked at it. A two-state model has no status\nfor \"done writing, waiting on a decision, locked\" — that is a third state.\n\n## Decision\n\nPost status is draft → pending → published. An ambassador can create, edit,\nand delete their own Post only while it is draft. Submitting moves it to\npending, which locks it from the author. An admin reviewing a pending Post\neither publishes it or bounces it back to draft for more edits. Only an admin\ncan move a Post into or out of published.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Every Post list, filter, and permission check in the codebase treats\n  pending as its own case — not as a synonym for draft (it is not\n  author-editable) or published (it is not public).\n- \"Nothing unapproved reaches the public site\" is enforced by restricting the\n  publish transition to admins, not by the pending state itself; pending is\n  what makes the hand-off visible and locks the author out while it waits.\n- The manual's own capability list says draft/published; this is a deliberate\n  extension to meet the client's explicit review-gate request, not a\n  deviation from what was asked for, and a future reader should expect three\n  Post statuses despite that wording.\n\n## Why this is an ADR\n\nHard to reverse: every status check, once built, assumes three states.\nSurprising without context: the manual itself only names two. Genuine\ntrade-off: two states is simpler and still meets the letter of capability 3,\nbut three is what the client's actual review workflow needs.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":947,"cache_read_input_tokens":95916,"output_tokens":789,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":947,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":789,"cache_read_input_tokens":95916,"cache_creation_input_tokens":947,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":947},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_016yJ7kKvSLcY9dZuwRD589L":{"file_path":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400/docs/adr/ADR-004-post-pending-status.md","content":"# ADR-004: Posts get a third status, pending, between draft and published\n\n**Status:** accepted\n**Date:** 2026-10-04\n\n## Context\n\nThe manual's capability 3 names only draft/published for Posts. {"parentUuid":"dfe64b00-af49-4248-8b28-42638aab03e0","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfiPXKoXDpK6bLpk2b3ML","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"`CONTEXT.md` now has Page, Post, Topic, Status, and Role defined, and `ADR-003`/`ADR-004` are written. Your answers resolved almost everything I was tracking — including Q1's rendering question, which your own phrasing (\"no special template features, they're just regular pages\") settled as a side effect: a Page's display is purely structural (list child Pages if any, list own Posts grouped by Topic if any), not a per-level template. One real fork is still open:\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q7** - **Does a Staff member's own post skip the review gate?**: ADR-004 gives every Post a draft → pending → published flow, and A3 says Staff have every tool Ambassadors have. When a Staff member writes their own Post, do they still go draft → submit → pending → (self-)publish, or does Staff's own draft show a direct **Publish** button, skipping pending entirely, since they're the one who'd be reviewing it anyway?\n\n➡️ Skip pending for Staff's own posts — draft → published directly. Pending exists to lock an *author* out while someone *else* decides; a Staff author reviewing their own work has nothing to lock against. Routing Staff through their own review queue would be a pure formality the brief never asked for, and it'd be one more state transition to build and test for no behavioral difference.\n\n---\n\nIf that matches your intent, the design tree's frontier is empty — let me know, and I'll treat this grill session as done and move on to the next stage (`/to-spec`) rather than opening new branches."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":921,"cache_read_input_tokens":96863,"output_tokens":496,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":921,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":496,"cache_read_input_tokens":96863,"cache_creation_input_tokens":921,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":921},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CfiPXKYQ4kwoyVkBMGKn9","type":"assistant","uuid":"52142137-f52c-4c51-9088-400a63136d09","timestamp":"2026-10-05T03:35:16.753Z","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

Only an admin can move a Post\ninto or out of published, and only an admin can bounce pending back to draft.\n_Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list\nnames only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit\nsubmit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004).","new_string":"**Status** (of a Post):\ndraft → pending → published. *Draft*: the author is still writing; only they\ncan edit it, and it is not public. *Pending*: the author has submitted it for\nreview and can no longer edit it; it is still not public — anyone with the\nadmin role can act on it, not just a specific reviewer, and there is no\nnotification when a Post lands in the queue. *Published*: live on the public\nsite. Only an admin can move a Post into or out of published, and only an\nadmin can bounce pending back to draft. One shortcut: an admin can publish\ntheir own draft directly, skipping pending, since there is no one else to\nreview it against; an admin's draft can also go through pending like anyone\nelse's if they want another admin's eyes on it first. The shortcut applies\nonly to an admin's own Post — an admin cannot push someone else's draft\nstraight to published without it passing through pending.\n_Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list\nnames only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit\nsubmit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004).","originalFile":"# Kenyon CGE Study Abroad CMS\n\nGlossary for the CMS built for the Kenyon Center for Global Engagement's study\nabroad blog. Client: `notes/client-brief.md`. The 7 fixed capabilities this\nvocabulary has to satisfy: `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` §3.3.\n\n## Language\n\n**Page**:\nSite content that sits in a fixed tree — Home, then Continent, then Country,\nthen Program — and appears in the public navigation once published. Rendering\nis uniform across every level: a Page lists its child Pages if it has any, and\nits own Posts grouped by Topic if it has any. There is no separate template per\nlevel. Staff add more Continents, Countries, and Programs later through the\nnormal page editor, the same way the seed set was created.\n_Avoid_: continent page, country page, program page as if they were distinct\ntypes — they are all just Pages at different places in the tree.\n\n**Post**:\nA dated blog entry written under a Program Page: title, slug, Markdown body,\nTopic, author, timestamps, and a status of draft, pending, or published.\n_Avoid_: entry, article.\n\n**Topic**:\nThe category a Post is tagged with, used to group and filter Posts on their\nProgram page like forum sections (read-only — no replies or discussion):\nGeneral, Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics, or Other.\n_Avoid_: \"hot topic\" as a separate concept from Topic — General is just one\nTopic value among the others, not a different kind of thing.\n\n**Status** (of a Post):\ndraft → pending → published. *Draft*: the author is still writing; only they\ncan edit it, and it is not public. *Pending*: the author has submitted it for\nreview and can no longer edit it; it is still not public. *Published*: CGE has\napproved it and it is live on the public site. Only an admin can move a Post\ninto or out of published, and only an admin can bounce pending back to draft.\n_Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list\nnames only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit\nsubmit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004).\n\n**Role**:\nTwo roles, per the manual: *admin*, shown in the UI as **Staff**, and *editor*,\nshown in the UI as **Ambassador**. The mapping is strict and permission-based,\nnot title-based — admin/editor stay the internal/code names (the manual's own\nvocabulary); Staff/Ambassador are what the site and this glossary call them.\nStaff have every capability Ambassadors have (they can write and submit Posts\ntoo) plus admin-only capabilities (publish, user management).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\" / \"student ambassador\" in place of Staff/Ambassador once\ninside the CMS's own vocabulary — those are brief language, not the product's.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":31,"oldLines":9,"newStart":31,"newLines":16,"lines":[" **Status** (of a Post):"," draft → pending → published. *Draft*: the author is still writing; only they"," can edit it, and it is not public. *Pending*: the author has submitted it for","-review and can no longer edit it; it is still not public. *Published*: CGE has","-approved it and it is live on the public site. Only an admin can move a Post","-into or out of published, and only an admin can bounce pending back to draft.","+review and can no longer edit it; it is still not public — anyone with the","+admin role can act on it, not just a specific reviewer, and there is no","+notification when a Post lands in the queue. *Published*: live on the public","+site. Only an admin can move a Post into or out of published, and only an","+admin can bounce pending back to draft. One shortcut: an admin can publish","+their own draft directly, skipping pending, since there is no one else to","+review it against; an admin's draft can also go through pending like anyone","+else's if they want another admin's eyes on it first. The shortcut applies","+only to an admin's own Post — an admin cannot push someone else's draft","+straight to published without it passing through pending."," _Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list"," names only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit"," submit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004)."]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"643c1d53-7496-4793-b83e-56ca38ad737a","session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

{"parentUuid":"933253b7-f061-42cb-8cd3-6162e24097cf","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfiPnbsLVNPamx7hboEbd","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Before closing the frontier, let me check it against your original field notes — the manual says those are meant to feed the grill, and two observations haven't been explicitly scoped yet. (Two others resolve on their own: field note 5's \"project comments\" is the same shape as the \"suggested edits\" feature A4/A5 already put in ADR-003, and field note 9's \"suite of user types\" is superseded by A3/A7's two-role model — Staff is simply a superset of Ambassador, not a step toward a richer permission system. Both worth saying out loud since field notes are graded raw material, not silently dropping them.)\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q8** - **Trash / soft-delete (field note 8)**: You liked WordPress sending deletions to a trash with a configurable auto-purge instead of deleting immediately. Capability 3 only requires delete (plain CRUD). In scope for MP2, or hard-delete only?\n\n➡️ Hard-delete only. This is exactly the shape of extra the manual's time budget (11–14 hrs for 7 fixed capabilities) argues against, and nothing in the brief or the 7 capabilities asks for it — it's a real improvement, just not this build's.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q9** - **Scheduled / visibility-gated publish (field note 3)**: You liked WordPress's publish dialog with public/private visibility and a future publish date. The draft/pending/published status already gives CGE a manual visibility gate. But a true *scheduled* future-dated auto-publish needs something running on its own to flip the status later — this project's `cms publish` is a manual, one-way step with no live process behind it (ADR-001). In scope as a non-functional \"planned date\" note, or out of scope entirely?\n\n➡️ Out of scope entirely, including as a cosmetic field. A date field that does nothing automatically would look like it works and doesn't — worse than not having it. If CGE wants a Post live on a specific day, they publish it that day."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1779,"cache_read_input_tokens":98404,"output_tokens":6098,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":5462},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1779,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":6098,"cache_read_input_tokens":98404,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1779,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1779},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CfiPnbcDFRbRnaD8V5mzi","type":"assistant","uuid":"c20dd41f-c296-4d18-8504-b143e0aa59f8","timestamp":"2026-10-05T03:39:48.004Z","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

Lists\nits own Posts, grouped by Topic, with a filter by Topic.\n\n**Post**:","originalFile":"# Kenyon CGE Study Abroad CMS\n\nGlossary for the CMS built for the Kenyon Center for Global Engagement's study\nabroad blog. Client: `notes/client-brief.md`. The 7 fixed capabilities this\nvocabulary has to satisfy: `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` §3.3.\n\n## Language\n\n**Page**:\nSite content that sits in a fixed tree — Home, then Continent, then Country,\nthen Program — and appears in the public navigation once published. Rendering\nis uniform across every level: a Page lists its child Pages if it has any, and\nits own Posts grouped by Topic if it has any. There is no separate template per\nlevel. Staff add more Continents, Countries, and Programs later through the\nnormal page editor, the same way the seed set was created.\n_Avoid_: continent page, country page, program page as if they were distinct\ntypes — they are all just Pages at different places in the tree.\n\n**Post**:\nA dated blog entry written under a Program Page: title, slug, Markdown body,\nTopic, author, timestamps, and a status of draft, pending, or published.\n_Avoid_: entry, article.\n\n**Topic**:\nThe category a Post is tagged with, used to group and filter Posts on their\nProgram page like forum sections (read-only — no replies or discussion):\nGeneral, Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics, or Other.\n_Avoid_: \"hot topic\" as a separate concept from Topic — General is just one\nTopic value among the others, not a different kind of thing.\n\n**Status** (of a Post):\ndraft → pending → published. *Draft*: the author is still writing; only they\ncan edit it, and it is not public. *Pending*: the author has submitted it for\nreview and can no longer edit it; it is still not public — anyone with the\nadmin role can act on it, not just a specific reviewer, and there is no\nnotification when a Post lands in the queue. *Published*: live on the public\nsite. Only an admin can move a Post into or out of published, and only an\nadmin can bounce pending back to draft. One shortcut: an admin can publish\ntheir own draft directly, skipping pending, since there is no one else to\nreview it against; an admin's draft can also go through pending like anyone\nelse's if they want another admin's eyes on it first. The shortcut applies\nonly to an admin's own Post — an admin cannot push someone else's draft\nstraight to published without it passing through pending.\n_Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list\nnames only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit\nsubmit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004).\n\n**Role**:\nTwo roles, per the manual: *admin*, shown in the UI as **Staff**, and *editor*,\nshown in the UI as **Ambassador**. The mapping is strict and permission-based,\nnot title-based — admin/editor stay the internal/code names (the manual's own\nvocabulary); Staff/Ambassador are what the site and this glossary call them.\nStaff have every capability Ambassadors have (they can write and submit Posts\ntoo) plus admin-only capabilities (publish, user management).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\" / \"student ambassador\" in place of Staff/Ambassador once\ninside the CMS's own vocabulary — those are brief language, not the product's.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":16,"oldLines":6,"newStart":16,"newLines":17,"lines":[" _Avoid_: continent page, country page, program page as if they were distinct"," types — they are all just Pages at different places in the tree."," ","+**Continent**:","+A Page one level below Home — Asia, Africa, and Europe in the seed data. Lists","+its child Country Pages.","+","+**Country**:","+A Page one level below a Continent. Lists its child Program Pages.","+","+**Program**:","+A Page one level below a Country — the level Posts are written under. Lists","+its own Posts, grouped by Topic, with a filter by Topic.","+"," **Post**:"," A dated blog entry written under a Program Page: title, slug, Markdown body,"," Topic, author, timestamps, and a status of draft, pending, or published."]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"dff88777-4366-40f5-9f6d-2d2a550d1189","session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

Client: `notes/client-brief.md`. The 7 fixed capabilities this\nvocabulary has to satisfy: `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` §3.3.\n\n## Language\n\n**Page**:\nSite content that sits in a fixed tree — Home, then Continent, then Country,\nthen Program — and appears in the public navigation once published. Rendering\nis uniform across every level: a Page lists its child Pages if it has any, and\nits own Posts grouped by Topic if it has any. There is no separate template per\nlevel. Staff add more Continents, Countries, and Programs later through the\nnormal page editor, the same way the seed set was created.\n_Avoid_: continent page, country page, program page as if they were distinct\ntypes — they are all just Pages at different places in the tree.\n\n**Continent**:\nA Page one level below Home — Asia, Africa, and Europe in the seed data. Lists\nits child Country Pages.\n\n**Country**:\nA Page one level below a Continent. Lists its child Program Pages.\n\n**Program**:\nA Page one level below a Country — the level Posts are written under. Lists\nits own Posts, grouped by Topic, with a filter by Topic.\n\n**Post**:\nA dated blog entry written under a Program Page: title, slug, Markdown body,\nTopic, author, timestamps, and a status of draft, pending, or published.\n_Avoid_: entry, article.\n\n**Topic**:\nThe category a Post is tagged with, used to group and filter Posts on their\nProgram page like forum sections (read-only — no replies or discussion):\nGeneral, Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics, or Other.\n_Avoid_: \"hot topic\" as a separate concept from Topic — General is just one\nTopic value among the others, not a different kind of thing.\n\n**Status** (of a Post):\ndraft → pending → published. *Draft*: the author is still writing; only they\ncan edit it, and it is not public. *Pending*: the author has submitted it for\nreview and can no longer edit it; it is still not public — anyone with the\nadmin role can act on it, not just a specific reviewer, and there is no\nnotification when a Post lands in the queue. *Published*: live on the public\nsite. Only an admin can move a Post into or out of published, and only an\nadmin can bounce pending back to draft. One shortcut: an admin can publish\ntheir own draft directly, skipping pending, since there is no one else to\nreview it against; an admin's draft can also go through pending like anyone\nelse's if they want another admin's eyes on it first. The shortcut applies\nonly to an admin's own Post — an admin cannot push someone else's draft\nstraight to published without it passing through pending.\n_Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list\nnames only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit\nsubmit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004).\n\n**Role**:\nTwo roles, per the manual: *admin*, shown in the UI as **Staff**, and *editor*,\nshown in the UI as **Ambassador**. The mapping is strict and permission-based,\nnot title-based — admin/editor stay the internal/code names (the manual's own\nvocabulary); Staff/Ambassador are what the site and this glossary call them.\nStaff have every capability Ambassadors have (they can write and submit Posts\ntoo) plus admin-only capabilities (publish, user management).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\" / \"student ambassador\" in place of Staff/Ambassador once\ninside the CMS's own vocabulary — those are brief language, not the product's.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":36,"oldLines":9,"newStart":36,"newLines":16,"lines":[" The category a Post is tagged with, used to group and filter Posts on their"," Program page like forum sections (read-only — no replies or discussion):"," General, Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics, or Other.","-_Avoid_: \"hot topic\" as a separate concept from Topic — General is just one","-Topic value among the others, not a different kind of thing.","+_Avoid_: treating General as a different kind of thing from the rest — see","+Hot Topic for how the two relate."," ","+**Hot Topic**:","+Any Topic value other than General — Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics,","+or Other. {"parentUuid":"38ccf870-667d-4e79-b883-0f7744daac63","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfiPwxy5sBwbWa2q5WwX8","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"CONTEXT.md now has Continent, Country, Program, Hot Topic, Staff, and Ambassador as their own entries, each cross-referencing Page/Topic/Role so nothing contradicts the earlier definitions. Here's the first of the four:\n\n❓ **Q10** - **How are slugs made, and can an Ambassador change theirs?**: Capability 3/4 requires a slug on every Post and Page, and field note 7 wanted it visible in the editor. Two parts: (a) is the slug auto-generated from the title (and only regenerated if the title changes before first save, or editable by hand at any time), and (b) can an Ambassador edit their own Post's slug, or is that a Staff-only field like it would be for a Page?\n\n➡️ Auto-generate from the title on first save, editable by hand after that by whoever can edit the content at all — so an Ambassador can adjust their own Post's slug while it's still draft (same window they can edit anything else in it), same as Staff can for a Page or for their own Post. No separate \"slug lock\" — the existing draft/pending/published edit-lock already covers it: once a Post leaves draft, its slug is as frozen as the rest of it."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":641,"cache_read_input_tokens":111436,"output_tokens":389,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":641,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":389,"cache_read_input_tokens":111436,"cache_creation_input_tokens":641,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":641},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CfiPwxckVnvr3LQ59wFtc","type":"assistant","uuid":"5980f990-241b-4507-87d9-fcbdaf4c5d42","timestamp":"2026-10-05T03:40:48.858Z","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

{"parentUuid":"b4d457f4-80c7-4a06-8af2-0e8e96fefb7e","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfiQXbRjZTZAM9KJgg8sE","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01HZZzZxazrgSYWZupnPLTYs","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400/notes/future-work.md","content":"# Future work\n\nFeatures worth building later, deliberately not in this build, and why —\nseparate from `docs/adr/`, because neither of these is a hard architectural\ntrade-off this project is locking in; they're just not worth their cost here.\n\n## Trash with restore and a 30-day auto-delete\n\nField note 8: WordPress sends a deleted Post/Page to a trash instead of\nremoving it, then purges it automatically after a configurable delay. Doing\nthe auto-purge half properly needs something running in the background to\ncheck ages and clear old entries on a schedule — and the admin console here\nonly runs when someone has it open (`uv run cms serve`), with nothing\nscheduled in between. A trash *without* the auto-purge is just a delayed,\nconfusing delete, so it's not worth building half the feature.\n\nFor now: plain delete, with an \"are you sure?\" confirmation before it runs\n(decided alongside this), so CGE doesn't lose a Post by accident — but once\ndeleted, it's gone.\n\n## Scheduled / visibility-gated publish\n\nField note 3: WordPress's publish dialog lets you set a future publish date\nand public/private visibility. The draft → pending → published status\nalready gives CGE a manual visibility gate (see `CONTEXT.md`). A *scheduled*\nfuture-dated auto-publish needs something to flip the status at the right\ntime with nobody watching — which this project doesn't have (`cms publish`\nis a manual, one-way step, ADR-001). A date field that doesn't actually\nschedule anything would look like it works and doesn't, which is worse than\nnot having it.\n\nFor now: if CGE wants a Post live on a specific day, they publish it that\nday.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1489,"cache_read_input_tokens":112801,"output_tokens":2537,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1877},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1489,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2537,"cache_read_input_tokens":112801,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1489,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1489},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01HZZzZxazrgSYWZupnPLTYs":{"file_path":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400/notes/future-work.md","content":"# Future work\n\nFeatures worth building later, deliberately not in this build, and why —\nseparate from `docs/adr/`, because neither of these is a hard architectural\ntrade-off this project is locking in; they're just not worth their cost here.\n\n## Trash with restore and a 30-day auto-delete\n\nField note 8: WordPress sends a deleted Post/Page to a trash instead of\nremoving it, then purges it automatically after a configurable delay. Doing\nthe auto-purge half properly needs something running in the background to\ncheck ages and clear old entries on a schedule — and the admin console here\nonly runs when someone has it open (`uv run cms serve`), with nothing\nscheduled in between. A trash *without* the auto-purge is just a delayed,\nconfusing delete, so it's not worth building half the feature.\n\nFor now: plain delete, with an \"are you sure?\" confirmation before it runs\n(decided alongside this), so CGE doesn't lose a Post by accident — but once\ndeleted, it's gone.\n\n## Scheduled / visibility-gated publish\n\nField note 3: WordPress's publish dialog lets you set a future publish date\nand public/private visibility. The draft → pending → published status\nalready gives CGE a manual visibility gate (see `CONTEXT.md`). A *scheduled*\nfuture-dated auto-publish needs something to flip the status at the right\ntime with nobody watching — which this project doesn't have (`cms publish`\nis a manual, one-way step, ADR-001).
