Nobody edits it by\nhand — it regenerates automatically whenever the title changes while the\ncontent is still draft, then freezes the moment it's published, so a shared\nlink never breaks. Shown read-only wherever the content is edited.\n_Avoid_: implying it's a form field a Staff or Ambassador fills in — it has\nno input of its own, only a display.","originalFile":"# Kenyon CGE Study Abroad CMS\n\nGlossary for the CMS built for the Kenyon Center for Global Engagement's study\nabroad blog. Client: `notes/client-brief.md`. The 7 fixed capabilities this\nvocabulary has to satisfy: `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` §3.3.\n\n## Language\n\n**Page**:\nSite content that sits in a fixed tree — Home, then Continent, then Country,\nthen Program — and appears in the public navigation once published. Rendering\nis uniform across every level: a Page lists its child Pages if it has any, and\nits own Posts grouped by Topic if it has any. There is no separate template per\nlevel. Staff add more Continents, Countries, and Programs later through the\nnormal page editor, the same way the seed set was created.\n_Avoid_: continent page, country page, program page as if they were distinct\ntypes — they are all just Pages at different places in the tree.\n\n**Continent**:\nA Page one level below Home — Asia, Africa, and Europe in the seed data. Lists\nits child Country Pages.\n\n**Country**:\nA Page one level below a Continent. Lists its child Program Pages.\n\n**Program**:\nA Page one level below a Country — the level Posts are written under. Lists\nits own Posts, grouped by Topic, with a filter by Topic.\n\n**Post**:\nA dated blog entry written under a Program Page: title, slug, Markdown body,\nTopic, author, timestamps, and a status of draft, pending, or published.\n_Avoid_: entry, article.\n\n**Topic**:\nThe category a Post is tagged with, used to group and filter Posts on their\nProgram page like forum sections (read-only — no replies or discussion):\nGeneral, Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics, or Other.\n_Avoid_: treating General as a different kind of thing from the rest — see\nHot Topic for how the two relate.\n\n**Hot Topic**:\nAny Topic value other than General — Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics,\nor Other. The brief and field notes' informal name for that subset; there is\nno separate field for it, only Topic.\n_Avoid_: treating Hot Topic as a type distinct from Topic, or as a field of\nits own — see Topic.\n\n**Status** (of a Post):\ndraft → pending → published. *Draft*: the author is still writing; only they\ncan edit it, and it is not public. *Pending*: the author has submitted it for\nreview and can no longer edit it; it is still not public — anyone with the\nadmin role can act on it, not just a specific reviewer, and there is no\nnotification when a Post lands in the queue. *Published*: live on the public\nsite. Only an admin can move a Post into or out of published, and only an\nadmin can bounce pending back to draft. One shortcut: an admin can publish\ntheir own draft directly, skipping pending, since there is no one else to\nreview it against; an admin's draft can also go through pending like anyone\nelse's if they want another admin's eyes on it first. The shortcut applies\nonly to an admin's own Post — an admin cannot push someone else's draft\nstraight to published without it passing through pending.\n_Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list\nnames only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit\nsubmit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004).\n\n**Role**:\nTwo roles, per the manual: *admin*, shown in the UI as **Staff**, and *editor*,\nshown in the UI as **Ambassador**. The mapping is strict and permission-based,\nnot title-based — admin/editor stay the internal/code names (the manual's own\nvocabulary); Staff/Ambassador are what the site and this glossary call them.\nStaff have every capability Ambassadors have (they can write and submit Posts\ntoo) plus admin-only capabilities (publish, user management).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\" / \"student ambassador\" in place of Staff/Ambassador once\ninside the CMS's own vocabulary — those are brief language, not the product's.\n\n**Staff**:\nThe UI-facing name for the admin role (see Role). Can manage users; create,\nedit, delete, and publish any Page or Post; and do everything an Ambassador\ncan, including writing and submitting their own Posts — with the option to\neither self-publish a draft directly or submit it to pending like anyone\nelse (see Status).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\", admin — see Role.\n\n**Ambassador**:\nThe UI-facing name for the editor role (see Role): a student who writes and\nsubmits their own Posts. Can create, edit, and delete only their own Posts,\nand only while draft (see Status); cannot touch another user's Post, cannot\ncreate or edit a Page, and cannot publish.\n_Avoid_: \"student ambassador\", editor — see Role.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":32,"oldLines":6,"newStart":32,"newLines":14,"lines":[" Topic, author, timestamps, and a status of draft, pending, or published."," _Avoid_: entry, article."," ","+**Slug**:","+The URL-safe name derived from a Post's or Page's title. Nobody edits it by","+hand — it regenerates automatically whenever the title changes while the","+content is still draft, then freezes the moment it's published, so a shared","+link never breaks. Shown read-only wherever the content is edited.","+_Avoid_: implying it's a form field a Staff or Ambassador fills in — it has","+no input of its own, only a display.","+"," **Topic**:"," The category a Post is tagged with, used to group and filter Posts on their"," Program page like forum sections (read-only — no replies or discussion):"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"b7aeded4-0f65-45c4-92eb-c4d8208ee6f3","session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

{"parentUuid":"de08a8c1-c0b3-44cc-863a-2a98c0a6459e","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfiQaMGXGq95jVKW6s7MC","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"`notes/future-work.md` now holds the deferred trash/restore and scheduled-publish ideas, and `CONTEXT.md` has a **Slug** entry recording that it's title-derived, regenerates only while draft, and freezes at publish — with the plain-delete-plus-confirmation decision noted for the spec stage. On to the second question:\n\n❓ **Q11** - **What happens to an Ambassador's account and Posts when they graduate / their term ends?**: Capability 6 requires deactivation, and a deactivated user can't log in — but that's silent on what happens to the account's existing Posts. Three parts: (a) do a graduated Ambassador's already-**published** Posts stay live, get unpublished, or get reassigned to a Staff author? (b) what about their **draft**/**pending** Posts that never got published — held as-is, or deleted? (c) is deactivation something CGE does manually when they know someone's abroad term ended, or does the brief suggest anything automatic (e.g., tied to a program end date)?\n\n➡️ (a) Published Posts stay live and keep the graduated Ambassador's byline — the brief's whole premise is \"real information... directly from other students who attended,\" so a post's value doesn't expire with its author's account. (b) Draft/pending Posts are left as-is, untouched, owned by the now-deactivated account — simplest rule, and if CGE wants one finished, they can always reactivate the account briefly rather than needing a reassignment feature. (c) Manual only — nothing in the brief ties account lifecycle to a program calendar, and building that would be inventing a requirement, not reading one."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":569,"cache_read_input_tokens":116947,"output_tokens":532,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":569,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":532,"cache_read_input_tokens":116947,"cache_creation_input_tokens":569,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":569},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CfiQaM1QZPvLhiPBJ3cfA","type":"assistant","uuid":"812a19ba-bb45-4f79-a566-cbc86fc46475","timestamp":"2026-10-05T03:49:04.321Z","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"bab46819-e189-4804-a8c5-5f2f464fcd08","timestamp":"2026-10-05T03:53:15.764Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400/CONTEXT.md","oldString":"only to an admin's own Post — an admin cannot push someone else's draft\nstraight to published without it passing through pending.\n_Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft","newString":"only to an admin's own Post — an admin cannot push someone else's draft\nstraight to published without it passing through pending. If the author's\naccount is later deactivated: a draft is deleted (nothing worth keeping from\nsomeone who's left, and it would otherwise clutter the content list); a\npending Post is left alone, since Staff still need to act on it; a published\nPost is left alone too and keeps its byline, since its value to readers has\nnothing to do with whether its author's account is still active.\n_Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft","originalFile":"# Kenyon CGE Study Abroad CMS\n\nGlossary for the CMS built for the Kenyon Center for Global Engagement's study\nabroad blog. Client: `notes/client-brief.md`. The 7 fixed capabilities this\nvocabulary has to satisfy: `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` §3.3.\n\n## Language\n\n**Page**:\nSite content that sits in a fixed tree — Home, then Continent, then Country,\nthen Program — and appears in the public navigation once published. Rendering\nis uniform across every level: a Page lists its child Pages if it has any, and\nits own Posts grouped by Topic if it has any. There is no separate template per\nlevel. Staff add more Continents, Countries, and Programs later through the\nnormal page editor, the same way the seed set was created.\n_Avoid_: continent page, country page, program page as if they were distinct\ntypes — they are all just Pages at different places in the tree.\n\n**Continent**:\nA Page one level below Home — Asia, Africa, and Europe in the seed data. Lists\nits child Country Pages.\n\n**Country**:\nA Page one level below a Continent. Lists its child Program Pages.\n\n**Program**:\nA Page one level below a Country — the level Posts are written under. Lists\nits own Posts, grouped by Topic, with a filter by Topic.\n\n**Post**:\nA dated blog entry written under a Program Page: title, slug, Markdown body,\nTopic, author, timestamps, and a status of draft, pending, or published.\n_Avoid_: entry, article.\n\n**Slug**:\nThe URL-safe name derived from a Post's or Page's title. Nobody edits it by\nhand — it regenerates automatically whenever the title changes while the\ncontent is still draft, then freezes the moment it's published, so a shared\nlink never breaks. Shown read-only wherever the content is edited.\n_Avoid_: implying it's a form field a Staff or Ambassador fills in — it has\nno input of its own, only a display.\n\n**Topic**:\nThe category a Post is tagged with, used to group and filter Posts on their\nProgram page like forum sections (read-only — no replies or discussion):\nGeneral, Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics, or Other.\n_Avoid_: treating General as a different kind of thing from the rest — see\nHot Topic for how the two relate.\n\n**Hot Topic**:\nAny Topic value other than General — Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics,\nor Other. The brief and field notes' informal name for that subset; there is\nno separate field for it, only Topic.\n_Avoid_: treating Hot Topic as a type distinct from Topic, or as a field of\nits own — see Topic.\n\n**Status** (of a Post):\ndraft → pending → published. *Draft*: the author is still writing; only they\ncan edit it, and it is not public. *Pending*: the author has submitted it for\nreview and can no longer edit it; it is still not public — anyone with the\nadmin role can act on it, not just a specific reviewer, and there is no\nnotification when a Post lands in the queue. *Published*: live on the public\nsite. Only an admin can move a Post into or out of published, and only an\nadmin can bounce pending back to draft. One shortcut: an admin can publish\ntheir own draft directly, skipping pending, since there is no one else to\nreview it against; an admin's draft can also go through pending like anyone\nelse's if they want another admin's eyes on it first. The shortcut applies\nonly to an admin's own Post — an admin cannot push someone else's draft\nstraight to published without it passing through pending.\n_Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list\nnames only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit\nsubmit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004).\n\n**Role**:\nTwo roles, per the manual: *admin*, shown in the UI as **Staff**, and *editor*,\nshown in the UI as **Ambassador**. The mapping is strict and permission-based,\nnot title-based — admin/editor stay the internal/code names (the manual's own\nvocabulary); Staff/Ambassador are what the site and this glossary call them.\nStaff have every capability Ambassadors have (they can write and submit Posts\ntoo) plus admin-only capabilities (publish, user management).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\" / \"student ambassador\" in place of Staff/Ambassador once\ninside the CMS's own vocabulary — those are brief language, not the product's.\n\n**Staff**:\nThe UI-facing name for the admin role (see Role). Can manage users; create,\nedit, delete, and publish any Page or Post; and do everything an Ambassador\ncan, including writing and submitting their own Posts — with the option to\neither self-publish a draft directly or submit it to pending like anyone\nelse (see Status).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\", admin — see Role.\n\n**Ambassador**:\nThe UI-facing name for the editor role (see Role): a student who writes and\nsubmits their own Posts. Can create, edit, and delete only their own Posts,\nand only while draft (see Status); cannot touch another user's Post, cannot\ncreate or edit a Page, and cannot publish.\n_Avoid_: \"student ambassador\", editor — see Role.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":66,"oldLines":7,"newStart":66,"newLines":12,"lines":[" review it against; an admin's draft can also go through pending like anyone"," else's if they want another admin's eyes on it first. The shortcut applies"," only to an admin's own Post — an admin cannot push someone else's draft","-straight to published without it passing through pending.","+straight to published without it passing through pending. If the author's","+account is later deactivated: a draft is deleted (nothing worth keeping from","+someone who's left, and it would otherwise clutter the content list); a","+pending Post is left alone, since Staff still need to act on it; a published","+Post is left alone too and keeps its byline, since its value to readers has","+nothing to do with whether its author's account is still active."," _Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list"," names only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit"," submit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004)."]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"19f247f4-c47d-49bb-8995-dde39f0b469c","session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

Most Pages sit in\nthe Continent → Country → Program tree below Home, but a Page can also stand\nalone under Home directly, like About CGE or Contact Us. Every Page's own\nbody lists its non-footer child Pages, if it has any, and its own Posts\ngrouped by Topic, if it has any — no separate template per level or per\nkind. A reader finds a Page three ways: the top nav bar (Home plus the\nContinents, always, regardless of what else exists), a breadcrumb trail\nbuilt from its parent chain (e.g. Home → Asia → Japan → Kenyon-in-Kyoto), and\nthe footer, which lists any Page with its \"show in footer\" flag checked — a\nfooter-flagged Page is left out of its parent's body listing so it isn't\nshown twice. Staff add more Continents, Countries, Programs, and standalone\nPages later through the normal page editor, the same way the seed set was\ncreated.\n_Avoid_: continent page, country page, program page as if they were distinct\ntypes — they are all just Pages at different places in the tree. Also avoid\nassuming every Page is travel content — About CGE and Contact Us are Pages\ntoo, just standalone ones under Home.","originalFile":"# Kenyon CGE Study Abroad CMS\n\nGlossary for the CMS built for the Kenyon Center for Global Engagement's study\nabroad blog. Client: `notes/client-brief.md`. The 7 fixed capabilities this\nvocabulary has to satisfy: `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` §3.3.\n\n## Language\n\n**Page**:\nSite content that sits in a fixed tree — Home, then Continent, then Country,\nthen Program — and appears in the public navigation once published. Rendering\nis uniform across every level: a Page lists its child Pages if it has any, and\nits own Posts grouped by Topic if it has any. There is no separate template per\nlevel. Staff add more Continents, Countries, and Programs later through the\nnormal page editor, the same way the seed set was created.\n_Avoid_: continent page, country page, program page as if they were distinct\ntypes — they are all just Pages at different places in the tree.\n\n**Continent**:\nA Page one level below Home — Asia, Africa, and Europe in the seed data. Lists\nits child Country Pages.\n\n**Country**:\nA Page one level below a Continent. Lists its child Program Pages.\n\n**Program**:\nA Page one level below a Country — the level Posts are written under. Lists\nits own Posts, grouped by Topic, with a filter by Topic.\n\n**Post**:\nA dated blog entry written under a Program Page: title, slug, Markdown body,\nTopic, author, timestamps, and a status of draft, pending, or published.\n_Avoid_: entry, article.\n\n**Slug**:\nThe URL-safe name derived from a Post's or Page's title. Nobody edits it by\nhand — it regenerates automatically whenever the title changes while the\ncontent is still draft, then freezes the moment it's published, so a shared\nlink never breaks. Shown read-only wherever the content is edited.\n_Avoid_: implying it's a form field a Staff or Ambassador fills in — it has\nno input of its own, only a display.\n\n**Topic**:\nThe category a Post is tagged with, used to group and filter Posts on their\nProgram page like forum sections (read-only — no replies or discussion):\nGeneral, Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics, or Other.\n_Avoid_: treating General as a different kind of thing from the rest — see\nHot Topic for how the two relate.\n\n**Hot Topic**:\nAny Topic value other than General — Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics,\nor Other. The brief and field notes' informal name for that subset; there is\nno separate field for it, only Topic.\n_Avoid_: treating Hot Topic as a type distinct from Topic, or as a field of\nits own — see Topic.\n\n**Status** (of a Post):\ndraft → pending → published. *Draft*: the author is still writing; only they\ncan edit it, and it is not public. *Pending*: the author has submitted it for\nreview and can no longer edit it; it is still not public — anyone with the\nadmin role can act on it, not just a specific reviewer, and there is no\nnotification when a Post lands in the queue. *Published*: live on the public\nsite. Only an admin can move a Post into or out of published, and only an\nadmin can bounce pending back to draft. One shortcut: an admin can publish\ntheir own draft directly, skipping pending, since there is no one else to\nreview it against; an admin's draft can also go through pending like anyone\nelse's if they want another admin's eyes on it first. The shortcut applies\nonly to an admin's own Post — an admin cannot push someone else's draft\nstraight to published without it passing through pending. If the author's\naccount is later deactivated: a draft is deleted (nothing worth keeping from\nsomeone who's left, and it would otherwise clutter the content list); a\npending Post is left alone, since Staff still need to act on it; a published\nPost is left alone too and keeps its byline, since its value to readers has\nnothing to do with whether its author's account is still active.\n_Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list\nnames only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit\nsubmit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004).\n\n**Role**:\nTwo roles, per the manual: *admin*, shown in the UI as **Staff**, and *editor*,\nshown in the UI as **Ambassador**. The mapping is strict and permission-based,\nnot title-based — admin/editor stay the internal/code names (the manual's own\nvocabulary); Staff/Ambassador are what the site and this glossary call them.\nStaff have every capability Ambassadors have (they can write and submit Posts\ntoo) plus admin-only capabilities (publish, user management).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\" / \"student ambassador\" in place of Staff/Ambassador once\ninside the CMS's own vocabulary — those are brief language, not the product's.\n\n**Staff**:\nThe UI-facing name for the admin role (see Role). Can manage users; create,\nedit, delete, and publish any Page or Post; and do everything an Ambassador\ncan, including writing and submitting their own Posts — with the option to\neither self-publish a draft directly or submit it to pending like anyone\nelse (see Status).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\", admin — see Role.\n\n**Ambassador**:\nThe UI-facing name for the editor role (see Role): a student who writes and\nsubmits their own Posts. Can create, edit, and delete only their own Posts,\nand only while draft (see Status); cannot touch another user's Post, cannot\ncreate or edit a Page, and cannot publish.\n_Avoid_: \"student ambassador\", editor — see Role.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":7,"oldLines":14,"newStart":7,"newLines":23,"lines":[" ## Language"," "," **Page**:","-Site content that sits in a fixed tree — Home, then Continent, then Country,","-then Program — and appears in the public navigation once published. Staff add more\nContinents, Countries, Programs, and standalone Pages later through the\nnormal page editor, the same way the seed set was created.","originalFile":"# Kenyon CGE Study Abroad CMS\n\nGlossary for the CMS built for the Kenyon Center for Global Engagement's study\nabroad blog. Client: `notes/client-brief.md`. The 7 fixed capabilities this\nvocabulary has to satisfy: `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` §3.3.\n\n## Language\n\n**Page**:\nSite content with a parent — except Home, which has none. Most Pages sit in\nthe Continent → Country → Program tree below Home, but a Page can also stand\nalone under Home directly, like About CGE or Contact Us. Every Page's own\nbody lists its non-footer child Pages, if it has any, and its own Posts\ngrouped by Topic, if it has any — no separate template per level or per\nkind. A reader finds a Page three ways: the top nav bar (Home plus the\nContinents, always, regardless of what else exists), a breadcrumb trail\nbuilt from its parent chain (e.g. Home → Asia → Japan → Kenyon-in-Kyoto), and\nthe footer, which lists any Page with its \"show in footer\" flag checked — a\nfooter-flagged Page is left out of its parent's body listing so it isn't\nshown twice. Staff add more Continents, Countries, Programs, and standalone\nPages later through the normal page editor, the same way the seed set was\ncreated.\n_Avoid_: continent page, country page, program page as if they were distinct\ntypes — they are all just Pages at different places in the tree. Also avoid\nassuming every Page is travel content — About CGE and Contact Us are Pages\ntoo, just standalone ones under Home.\n\n**Continent**:\nA Page one level below Home — Asia, Africa, and Europe in the seed data. Lists\nits child Country Pages.\n\n**Country**:\nA Page one level below a Continent. Lists its child Program Pages.\n\n**Program**:\nA Page one level below a Country — the level Posts are written under. Lists\nits own Posts, grouped by Topic, with a filter by Topic.\n\n**Post**:\nA dated blog entry written under a Program Page: title, slug, Markdown body,\nTopic, author, timestamps, and a status of draft, pending, or published.\n_Avoid_: entry, article.\n\n**Slug**:\nThe URL-safe name derived from a Post's or Page's title. Nobody edits it by\nhand — it regenerates automatically whenever the title changes while the\ncontent is still draft, then freezes the moment it's published, so a shared\nlink never breaks. Shown read-only wherever the content is edited.\n_Avoid_: implying it's a form field a Staff or Ambassador fills in — it has\nno input of its own, only a display.\n\n**Topic**:\nThe category a Post is tagged with, used to group and filter Posts on their\nProgram page like forum sections (read-only — no replies or discussion):\nGeneral, Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics, or Other.\n_Avoid_: treating General as a different kind of thing from the rest — see\nHot Topic for how the two relate.\n\n**Hot Topic**:\nAny Topic value other than General — Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics,\nor Other. The brief and field notes' informal name for that subset; there is\nno separate field for it, only Topic.\n_Avoid_: treating Hot Topic as a type distinct from Topic, or as a field of\nits own — see Topic.\n\n**Status** (of a Post):\ndraft → pending → published. *Draft*: the author is still writing; only they\ncan edit it, and it is not public. *Pending*: the author has submitted it for\nreview and can no longer edit it; it is still not public — anyone with the\nadmin role can act on it, not just a specific reviewer, and there is no\nnotification when a Post lands in the queue. *Published*: live on the public\nsite. Only an admin can move a Post into or out of published, and only an\nadmin can bounce pending back to draft. One shortcut: an admin can publish\ntheir own draft directly, skipping pending, since there is no one else to\nreview it against; an admin's draft can also go through pending like anyone\nelse's if they want another admin's eyes on it first. The shortcut applies\nonly to an admin's own Post — an admin cannot push someone else's draft\nstraight to published without it passing through pending. If the author's\naccount is later deactivated: a draft is deleted (nothing worth keeping from\nsomeone who's left, and it would otherwise clutter the content list); a\npending Post is left alone, since Staff still need to act on it; a published\nPost is left alone too and keeps its byline, since its value to readers has\nnothing to do with whether its author's account is still active.\n_Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list\nnames only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit\nsubmit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004).\n\n**Role**:\nTwo roles, per the manual: *admin*, shown in the UI as **Staff**, and *editor*,\nshown in the UI as **Ambassador**. The mapping is strict and permission-based,\nnot title-based — admin/editor stay the internal/code names (the manual's own\nvocabulary); Staff/Ambassador are what the site and this glossary call them.\nStaff have every capability Ambassadors have (they can write and submit Posts\ntoo) plus admin-only capabilities (publish, user management).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\" / \"student ambassador\" in place of Staff/Ambassador once\ninside the CMS's own vocabulary — those are brief language, not the product's.\n\n**Staff**:\nThe UI-facing name for the admin role (see Role). Can manage users; create,\nedit, delete, and publish any Page or Post; and do everything an Ambassador\ncan, including writing and submitting their own Posts — with the option to\neither self-publish a draft directly or submit it to pending like anyone\nelse (see Status).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\", admin — see Role.\n\n**Ambassador**:\nThe UI-facing name for the editor role (see Role): a student who writes and\nsubmits their own Posts. Can create, edit, and delete only their own Posts,\nand only while draft (see Status); cannot touch another user's Post, cannot\ncreate or edit a Page, and cannot publish.\n_Avoid_: \"student ambassador\", editor — see Role.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":9,"oldLines":17,"newStart":9,"newLines":18,"lines":[" **Page**:"," Site content with a parent — except Home, which has none. {"parentUuid":"809aa2e6-8aa5-4727-9831-f75d6f6355f5","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"49a02977-0f70-4573-9ab9-3bd9d5fc3e56","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01R6yxJsLiFxBUyKkYHTzksd","type":"tool_result","content":"=== issue-tracker.md ===\n# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\n=== domain.md ===\n# Domain Docs\n\nHow the engineering skills should consume this repo's domain documentation when exploring the codebase.\n\n## Before exploring, read these\n\n- **`CONTEXT.md`** at the repo root, or\n- **`CONTEXT-MAP.md`** at the repo root if it exists: it points at one `CONTEXT.md` per context. Read each one relevant to the topic.\n- **`docs/adr/`**: read ADRs that touch the area you're about to work in. In multi-context repos, also check `src/<context>/docs/adr/` for context-scoped decisions.\n\nIf any of these files don't exist, **proceed silently**. Don't flag their absence; don't suggest creating them upfront. The `/domain-modeling` skill (reached via `/grill-with-docs` and `/improve-codebase-architecture`) creates them lazily when terms or decisions actually get resolved.\n\n## File structure\n\nSingle-context repo (most repos):\n\n```\n/\n├── CONTEXT.md\n├── docs/adr/\n│   ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md\n│   └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md\n└── src/\n```\n\nMulti-context repo (presence of `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the root):\n\n```\n/\n├── CONTEXT-MAP.md\n├── docs/adr/                          ← system-wide decisions\n└── src/\n    ├── ordering/\n    │   ├── CONTEXT.md\n    │   └── docs/adr/                  ← context-specific decisions\n    └── billing/\n        ├── CONTEXT.md\n        └── docs/adr/\n```\n\n## Use the glossary's vocabulary\n\nWhen your output names a domain concept (in an issue title, a refactor proposal, a hypothesis, a test name), use the term as defined in `CONTEXT.md`. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. {"parentUuid":"96e800a7-be97-4a72-a0fb-b09760dad38d","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"49a02977-0f70-4573-9ab9-3bd9d5fc3e56","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0141ioeHqe2Ud6zGJ1CdTxAq","type":"tool_result","content":"=== app/main.py ===\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nT00 (already done): the admin console answers at /admin and the public site\nanswers at /. That is the whole skeleton — it exists so you can prove the stack\nruns before you build anything on it.\n\nAdd your routes in their own modules (app/routes/posts.py and so on) and include\nthem here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import settings\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/admin\")\n    def admin_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\"}\n        )\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    # Your ticket work plugs in here, e.g.\n    #   from app.routes import posts\n    #   app.include_router(posts.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n=== app/cli.py ===\n\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"deploy\":\n        if not settings.SITE.exists():\n            print(\"site/ does not exist yet — run `uv run cms publish` first.\")\n            return 1\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", args.message,\n             str(settings.SITE)],\n        )\n        if result.returncode == 0:\n            print(\"Pushed to gh-pages. Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> \"\n                  \"gh-pages / root, then wait up to 10 minutes.\")\n        return result.returncode\n    return 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n=== app/publish.py ===\n\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[], css_path=\"style.css\",\n            home_path=\"index.html\",\n        )\n    )\n    return out\n=== app/settings.py ===\n\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\nSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n\nSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\nDATABASE_PATH = Path(os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", ROOT / \"cms.db\"))\nSITE_TITLE = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\", \"My CMS\")\n# Set this to your Pages URL once you deploy, e.g.\n# https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nBASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"153f816a-09ec-430c-9ee4-cec85ac7e0b7","timestamp":"2026-10-05T04:11:17.271Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"=== app/main.py ===\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nT00 (already done): the admin console answers at /admin and the public site\nanswers at /. }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[], css_path=\"style.css\",\n            home_path=\"index.html\",\n        )\n    )\n    return out\n=== app/settings.py ===\n\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\nSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n\nSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\nDATABASE_PATH = Path(os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", ROOT / \"cms.db\"))\nSITE_TITLE = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\", \"My CMS\")\n# Set this to your Pages URL once you deploy, e.g.\n# https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nBASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"96e800a7-be97-4a72-a0fb-b09760dad38d","session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client() -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as():\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(create_app())\n        response = c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": user[\"email\"],\n                                          \"password\": user[\"password\"]},\n                          follow_redirects=False)\n        if response.status_code == 404:\n            pytest.skip(\"No /login route yet — build the login ticket first.\")\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n=== test_t00.py ===\n\"\"\"T00: the walking skeleton.  assert \"hello admin\" in response.text.lower()\n\n\ndef test_public_home_answers(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/\")\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n\n\ndef test_publish_writes_a_site(tmp_path):\n    from app.publish import render_site\n\n    out = render_site(tmp_path / \"site\")\n    assert (out / \"index.html\").exists() and (out / \"style.css\").exists()\n\n\ndef test_published_html_uses_relative_paths(tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"Root-absolute paths break on GitHub Pages project URLs (rubric F2).\"\"\"\n    from app.publish import \"fastapi>=0.115\",\n    \"uvicorn[standard]>=0.32\",\n    \"jinja2>=3.1\",\n    \"python-multipart>=0.0.12\",   # form posts\n    \"itsdangerous>=2.2\",          # signed session cookies\n    \"argon2-cffi>=23.1\",          # password hashing (never store plain passwords)\n    \"markdown-it-py>=3.0\",        # Markdown -> HTML\n    \"nh3>=0.2\",                   # HTML sanitizer (strips <script> etc.)\n    \"ghp-import>=2.1\",            # push site/ to the gh-pages branch\n]\n\n[dependency-groups]\ndev = [\"pytest>=8.3\", \"httpx>=0.28\"]\n\n[project.scripts]\ncms = <title>{% block title %}{{ title }}{% endblock %}</title>\n  <link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"{{ css_path | default('style.css') }}\">\n</head>\n<body>\n  <header><a href=\"{{ home_path | default('index.html') }}\">{{ title }}</a></header>\n  <main>{% block content %}{% endblock %}</main>\n  <footer><small>IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2</small></footer>\n</body>\n</html>\n=== SECURITY-CHECKLIST ===\n# Security checklist\n\nWhat must be true before you submit. *How* to make each one true is your work —\nthat is the point of the tickets.\n\n| # | Must be true | How the grader checks it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Stored passwords are argon2 hashes | Reads the seeded database and looks at the stored value |\n| 2 | Wrong passwords are refused, and the message does not reveal whether the account exists | Tries a bad password |\n| 3 | Every state-changing form (POST) carries a CSRF token and rejects a request without one | Replays each POST with the token removed |\n| 4 | An editor cannot reach any admin-only route | Logs in as the seeded editor and requests each admin route |\n| 5 | An anonymous visitor is redirected to login, never shown admin content | Requests admin routes with no session |\n| 6 | A deactivated user cannot log in | Deactivates the seeded editor, then tries to log in |\n| 7 | User-written Markdown cannot inject scripts | Saves a post containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute, publishes, and checks both the preview and the export |\n| 8 | Drafts never appear in `site/` or on the public site | Publishes with a draft present and searches the output |\n| 9 | No secrets, databases, or `.env` files in git history | Greps the full history |\n| 10 | Access control is enforced in code, not by hiding links | Requests admin URLs directly rather than clicking |\n\nRule of thumb: if the only thing stopping an editor from reaching a page is that\nthe link is hidden, it is not stopping | Must be true | How the grader checks it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Stored passwords are argon2 hashes | Reads the seeded database and looks at the stored value |\n| 2 | Wrong passwords are refused, and the message does not reveal whether the account exists | Tries a bad password |\n| 3 | Every state-changing form (POST) carries a CSRF token and rejects a request without one | Replays each POST with the token removed |\n| 4 | An editor cannot reach any admin-only route | Logs in as the seeded editor and requests each admin route |\n| 5 | An anonymous visitor is redirected to login, never shown admin content | Requests admin routes with no session |\n| 6 | A deactivated user cannot log in | Deactivates the seeded editor, then tries to log in |\n| 7 | User-written Markdown cannot inject scripts | Saves a post containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute, publishes, and checks both the preview and the export |\n| 8 | Drafts never appear in `site/` or on the public site | Publishes with a draft present and searches the output |\n| 9 | No secrets, databases, or `.env` files in git history | Greps the full history |\n| 10 | Access control is enforced in code, not by hiding links | Requests admin URLs directly rather than clicking |\n\nRule of thumb: if the only thing stopping an editor from reaching a page is that\nthe link is hidden, it is not stopping anyone.","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"68f6fcee-0033-4dfd-9417-ce8ebae1545f","session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

As you build content types, extend this so it creates:\n  - one admin and one editor (passwords read from .env, never hard-coded)\n  - a few posts and pages, at least one draft and one published\n\nThe rubric expects this to run clean on a fresh clone with .env.example values\n(item E4), because the database itself is never committed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    admin_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\")\n    editor_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\")\n    if not admin_pw or not editor_pw:\n        print(\"Set CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD in .env \"\n              \"(copy .env.example).\")\n        return 1\n\n    # TODO (your tickets): create the users, then the demo content.\n    print(\"Nothing to seed yet: no content types exist. \"\n          \"Extend scripts/seed_demo.py as you build T01+.\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n=== templates/public/home.html ===\n{% extends \"base.html\" %}\n{% block content %}\n  <h1>{{ title }}</h1>\n  {% if items %}\n    <ul>{% for item in items %}<li><a href=\"{{ item.href }}\">{{ item.title }}</a></li>{% endfor %}</ul>\n  {% else %}\n    <p>Nothing published yet.</p>\n  {% endif %}\n{% endblock %}\n=== templates/admin/hello.html ===\n{% extends \"base.html\" %}\n{% block content %}\n  <h1>T00: hello admin</h1>\n  <p>The stack works. --- checks -----------------------------------------------------------\n    def hygiene(self) -> None:\n        tracked = sh(\"git\", \"ls-files\").splitlines()\n        bad = [f for f in tracked if f.endswith((\".db\", \".env\")) or f.startswith(\".claude/state/\")]\n        self.add(not bad, \"no database or .env committed\", \", \".join(bad) or \"clean\",\n                 \"git rm --cached <file>, confirm .gitignore covers it, then rewrite history if it is old\")\n        history = sh(\"git\", \"log\", \"--all\", \"-p\", \"--\", \".\")\n        hits = sorted(set(SECRET.findall(history)))\n        self.add(not hits, \"no secrets in history\", f\"{len(hits)} match(es)\",\n                 \"rotate the key first, then ask Claude to rewrite history\")\n        self.add((ROOT / \".env.example\").exists(), \".env.example present\", \"\", \"restore it from the template\")\n\n    def docs(self, stage: int) -> None:\n        pairs = [\n            (\"notes/cms-field-notes.md\", \"field notes\"),\n            (\"CONTEXT.md\", \"glossary\"),\n            (\"notes/token-budget-plan.md\", \"token budget plan\"),\n            (\"notes/usage-ledger.csv\", \"usage ledger\"),\n            (\"docs/process/compaction-log.md\", \"compaction log\"),\n        ]\n        if stage >= 2:\n            pairs += [(\"README.md\", \"README\"), (\"scripts/seed_demo.py\", \"seed script\")]\n        for path, label in pairs:","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"8a9a8b7a-88bd-4746-93d6-0a95cc31672d","timestamp":"2026-10-05T04:11:27.879Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Create demo data so a grader (and you) can use the CMS immediately.\n\n    uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py\n\nT00 has nothing to seed. Now build ticket T01.</p>\n{% endblock %}\n=== check_submission.py (head) ===\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Check your submission before you send it. The judge runs this first.\n\n    uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 1\n    uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2\n    uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2 --json\n\nStage 0 is the instructor's check of the template itself.\nExit code 0 means every check passed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport re\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nSECRET = re.compile(r\"(sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}|ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN\\s*[:=]\\s*\\S{8,}|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY)\")\nREPORT = re.compile(r\"^iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_[a-z]+-[a-z-]+_\\d{8}\\.md$\")\nTRANSCRIPT = re.compile(r\"^iphs400_mp2-cms_chat-session_\\d{2}_[a-z]+-[a-z-]+_\\d{8}\\.md$\")\nSCREENS = [\"login\", \"dashboard\", \"content-list\", \"editor\", \"users\", \"editor-denied\"]\n\n\ndef sh(*args: str) -> str:\n    return subprocess.run(args, cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout\n\n\nclass Checks:\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self.results: list[dict] = []\n\n    def add(self, ok: bool, name: str, detail: str, fix: str = \"\") -> None:\n        self.results.append({\"check\": name, \"ok\": bool(ok), \"detail\": detail, \"fix\": fix})\n\n    # --- checks -----------------------------------------------------------\n    def hygiene(self) -> None:\n        tracked = sh(\"git\", \"ls-files\").splitlines()\n        bad = [f for f in tracked if f.endswith((\".db\", \".env\")) or f.startswith(\".claude/state/\")]\n        self.add(not bad, \"no database or .env committed\", \", \".join(bad) or \"clean\",\n                 \"git rm --cached <file>, confirm .gitignore covers it, then rewrite history if it is old\")\n        history = sh(\"git\", \"log\", \"--all\", \"-p\", \"--\", \".\")\n        hits = sorted(set(SECRET.findall(history)))\n        self.add(not hits, \"no secrets in history\", f\"{len(hits)} match(es)\",\n                 \"rotate the key first, then ask Claude to rewrite history\")\n        self.add((ROOT / \".env.example\").exists(), \".env.example present\", \"\", \"restore it from the template\")\n\n    def docs(self, stage: int) -> None:\n        pairs = [\n            (\"notes/cms-field-notes.md\", \"field notes\"),\n            (\"CONTEXT.md\", \"glossary\"),\n            (\"notes/token-budget-plan.md\", \"token budget plan\"),\n            (\"notes/usage-ledger.csv\", \"usage ledger\"),\n            (\"docs/process/compaction-log.md\", \"compaction log\"),\n        ]\n        if stage >= 2:\n            pairs += [(\"README.md\", \"README\"), (\"scripts/seed_demo.py\", \"seed script\")]\n        for path, label in pairs:","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"6449de04-fd52-4702-a4ca-848fb5b08c2b","session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

{"parentUuid":"b50916c8-ac72-4e6d-a13c-43ae1afdd017","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfiSbytgs17DSpKSXTRUe","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01XCCYd3GX3LzjCZuHPQfaqB","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > /tmp/claude-1000/-home-adam-leider-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-CMS-Project-IPHS-400/eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce/scratchpad/spec-body.md << 'SPECEOF'\n## Problem Statement\n\nKenyon students researching study-abroad programs currently have to rely on outside sites that are poorly maintained and hard to search for specific answers (housing, meals, social life, academics). The Kenyon Center for Global Engagement (CGE) wants its own site where student Ambassadors who've actually attended a program write about it, but CGE must review every post before it goes public — nothing unapproved can reach a reader, and an Ambassador must never be able to touch anyone else's writing or the site's structure.\n\n## Solution\n\nA CMS with two roles — **Staff** (admin) and **Ambassador** (editor), see `CONTEXT.md` — where Ambassadors write and submit Posts, Staff review and publish them, and the public site is a static export organized as Home → Continent → Country → Program, with Posts grouped and filterable by Topic on their Program page. `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/ADR-003`, `ADR-004` are the settled vocabulary and decisions this spec builds on; `notes/future-work.md` lists what's deliberately deferred.\n\n## User Stories\n\n**Login (capability 1)**\n1. As a Staff member, I want to log in with my email and password, so that I can access the admin console.\n2. As an Ambassador, I want to log in with my email and password, so that I can write and manage my own posts.\n3. As any user, I want a wrong password refused without the response revealing whether the account exists, so that no one can probe for valid emails.\n4. As a deactivated user, I want my login refused, so that I can't access the system after my account is deactivated.\n5. As any logged-in user, I want to log out, so that I can end my session on a shared computer.\n\n**Roles (capability 2)**\n6. As a Staff member, I want every Ambassador capability available to me too, so that I can write and submit my own Posts without a second account.\n7. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from any admin-only route, so that I can't reach user management or page authoring.\n8. As an anonymous visitor, I want to be redirected to login when I request an admin route, so that the admin console stays private.\n\n**Posts: authoring and the review gate (capability 3, ADR-004)**\n9. As an Ambassador, I want to create a new draft Post under a Program, so that I can start writing about my experience there.\n10. As an Ambassador, I want to edit my own draft Post's title, body, and Topic, so that I can revise it before submitting.\n11. As an Ambassador, I want to delete my own draft Post, after confirming \"are you sure?\", so that I don't lose it to a misclick but can still abandon it.\n12. As an Ambassador, I want to submit my draft for review, so that CGE can decide whether to publish it.\n13. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from editing or deleting my Post once it's pending or published, so that nothing changes mid-review or after it's live without CGE knowing.\n14. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from touching another Ambassador's Post in any way, so that I can't edit, delete, or resubmit someone else's writing.\n15. As a Staff member, I want to publish a pending Post, so that it goes live on the public site.\n16. As a Staff member, I want to bounce a pending Post back to draft, so that its author can revise it before I reconsider.\n17. As a Staff member, I want to publish my own draft Post directly, so that I don't have to route my own work through a review queue.\n18. As a Staff member, I want the option to submit my own Post to pending instead, so that another Staff member can review it first.\n19. As a Staff member, I want to edit or delete any Post regardless of status or author, so that I can fix a problem or remove content without waiting on anyone.\n20. As a Staff member, I want to unpublish a live Post back to draft, so that I can pull it down for a larger rewrite.\n\n**Pages and the content tree (capability 4)**\n21. As a Staff member, I want to create a Page nested under an existing Page (Home, a Continent, or a Country), so that I can build out the Continent → Country → Program tree.\n22. As a Staff member, I want to create a standalone Page directly under Home (e.g. \"About CGE\"), so that I can publish information that isn't travel content.\n23. As a Staff member, I want to flag a Page to show in the footer, so that standalone pages are reachable without cluttering the main navigation.\n24. As a Staff member, I want to edit or delete any Page, so that I can keep the site's structure current as programs change.\n25. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from creating, editing, or deleting any Page, so that the site's structure stays under CGE's control.\n\n**Topic (ADR-004 scope note, field notes)**\n26. As a visitor reading a Program page, I want its Posts grouped by Topic, so that I can jump straight to Housing or Academics instead of scrolling through everything.\n27. As a visitor reading a Program page, I want to filter to one Topic or see everything, so that I only see what I'm looking for.\n28. As an Ambassador, I want to tag my Post with a Topic when I write it, so that it lands in the right section of the Program page.\n\n**Public navigation (field notes, client brief)**\n29. As a visitor on any public page, I want a nav bar with Home and the Continents, so that I can jump to a different region from anywhere.\n30. As a visitor drilled into a Program page, I want a breadcrumb trail (Home → Continent → Country → Program), so that I can see where I am and step back up a level at a time.\n31. As a visitor, I want a footer linking to standalone pages like \"About CGE\" and \"Contact Us\", so that I can find that information from anywhere on the site.\n32. As a visitor on a phone, I want the nav bar to wrap or collapse, so that it never runs off the screen.\n\n**Admin console (capability 5)**\n33. As a Staff member, I want my admin home screen to be a live preview of the site, so that I land on what's actually published, the way WordPress's own admin works.\n34. As a Staff member, I want a Dashboard tab with counts (Posts by status, Pages by level, active accounts), so that I can see the state of the whole site at a glance.\n35. As a Staff member, I want a Pending queue tab listing every Post waiting on a decision, so that nothing sits unreviewed because no one thought to check.\n36. As a Staff member, I want a Metrics tab showing Posts per Program, so that I can see which programs have no Ambassador content yet.\n37. As an Ambassador, I want a \"My posts\" view listing my own drafts, pending, and published Posts, so that I can track what I've written without seeing anyone else's.\n\n**User management (capability 6)**\n38. As a Staff member, I want an Accounts tab to create users, assign a role, and activate/deactivate an account, so that I can manage who has access.\n39. As a Staff member, I want a deactivated user's draft Posts (and draft Pages, if they held the Staff role) deleted automatically, so that the content list doesn't fill up with abandoned half-finished work.\n40. As a Staff member, I want a deactivated user's pending and published content left exactly as it is, so that I can still publish what's in the queue and readers keep seeing valuable published content.\n41. As a visitor, I want a published Post to keep showing its original author's name even after that account is deactivated, so that the byline stays honest.\n\n**Public site and publish (capability 7)**\n42. As a Staff member, I want `cms publish` to write only published Posts and Pages into `site/`, so that nothing in draft or pending ever leaks to the public.\n43. As a Staff member, I want every link and asset in the exported HTML to be relative, so that the site works on its GitHub Pages subpath.\n44. As a visitor, I want a Post's Markdown rendered as sanitized HTML, so that nothing an Ambassador wrote can inject a script into the page I'm reading.\n45. As a Staff member, I want a slug frozen the instant something is published, so that a link a reader has already shared never breaks.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n**Module split** (new, per this spec): `app/models.py` — plain SQLite access (no ORM, per ADR-002), `User`/`Page`/`Post` reads and writes. `app/services/` — pure rules with no FastAPI or SQLite dependency: slug generation, the status state machine, the deactivation cascade. `app/routes/` — thin HTTP handlers that call services for decisions and models for persistence. `templates/` — unchanged, `admin/` and `public/` subtrees as already established.\n\n**Data model** (logical, fields not file-bound):\n- `User`: id, email, password_hash (argon2), role (`admin`/`editor`), display_name, active (bool), timestamps.\n- `Page`: id, parent_id (nullable only for Home), title, slug, body (Markdown), status (`draft`/`published` — **no `pending`**: only Staff author Pages, and Staff can self-publish, so there's never a reviewer to wait on), `show_in_footer` (bool), author_id, timestamps, published_at.\n- `Post`: id, program_id (must reference a Program-level Page), title, slug, body (Markdown), topic (`general`/`housing`/`meals`/`social-life`/`academics`/`other`), status (`draft`/`pending`/`published`), author_id, timestamps, published_at.\n\n**Status state machine** (services layer; a decision this precise is clearer as a table than prose):\n\n| From | Action | Who | To |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| draft | submit | the Post's own author (any role) | pending |\n| pending | publish | any admin | published |\n| pending | bounce | any admin | draft |\n| draft | self-publish | admin, **own Post only** | published |\n| published | unpublish | any admin | draft |\n\nNo other transition exists. In particular, an admin cannot move *someone else's* draft straight to published — it must be submitted to pending first, same as anyone's. This keeps \"an Ambassador's post is never published without someone deciding to put it through pending\" true even when the decider is an admin, not just an Ambassador.\n\n**Content edit/delete permission** (orthogonal to status, from `CONTEXT.md`'s Staff/Ambassador entries): admin — any Post or Page, any status, always. Editor — only their own Post, only while draft. Never any Page.\n\n**Slug generation**: derived from title (lowercase, non-alphanumeric runs collapsed to hyphens). Regenerates on every title change while status is draft; frozen the moment status leaves draft, even if an admin edits the title afterward. On a collision with a sibling under the same parent, append `-2`, `-3`, â€¦ — not grilled explicitly; flagged below.\n\n**Deactivation cascade** (services layer): on deactivating any user (Staff or Ambassador), delete their draft Posts and, if they held the Staff role, their draft Pages. Leave pending and published content untouched, byline intact. The grill settled this for Ambassadors specifically (A11); extending it uniformly to a deactivated Staff account is a synthesis decision, flagged below.\n\n**Public URL / nav contract**: a Page's public path is the slug chain of its ancestors from Home (Home = site root); a Post's path nests under its Program's path. A footer-flagged standalone Page still gets a path under Home, just excluded from Home's own child listing (`CONTEXT.md`, Page).\n\n**Admin console layout**: Staff's landing screen is a live preview of the site inside the console; sidebar tabs are Dashboard, Pending queue, Accounts, Page hierarchy, Metrics. Ambassador's sidebar is just \"My posts\". No reviewer assignment and no notifications on the pending queue — any admin can act on any pending Post.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\nA good test asserts externally observable behavior — status code, redirect target, response HTML, a written file's contents, or a service function's return value/raised error — never an internal implementation detail.\n\n- **HTTP seam** (`TestClient`, prior art: `tests/test_t00.py`, `conftest.py`'s `client_as(role)`): login success/failure/deactivated, every admin-only route rejected for an editor and for an anonymous request, Post/Page CRUD and every status-transition route end-to-end, CSRF rejection on a POST with the token stripped, the Dashboard/Pending-queue/Accounts/Metrics/My-posts screens, nav bar/breadcrumb/footer HTML on public pages.\n- **`render_site()` seam** (prior art: `test_publish_writes_a_site`, `test_published_html_uses_relative_paths`): a draft or pending Post/Page present but absent from the output, every href/src relative, sanitized Markdown in the exported HTML, a frozen slug surviving a post-publish title edit, nav/breadcrumb/footer present in the static files.\n- **Services seam** (new, no HTTP or DB — plain pytest functions): every cell of the status state-machine table including the disallowed combinations (e.g. editor attempting publish, admin attempting draft→published on someone else's Post), slug generation and its collision suffixing, the deactivation cascade's decision of which Posts/Pages to delete vs. keep.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nPer ADR-003: private messaging, a visitor/commenter account role, an IT/developer role, view/comment-based search filters, in-CMS suggested-edit tooling. Per `notes/future-work.md`: trash/restore with a 30-day auto-delete (plain delete only, with a confirmation prompt), scheduled/visibility-gated publish.
