{"parentUuid":"0fc3d190-aa0f-4d1c-9235-77f2b0a50843","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"edited_text_file","filename":"/tmp/claude-1000/-home-adam-leider-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-CMS-Project-IPHS-400/eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce/scratchpad/spec-body.md","snippet":"1\t## Problem Statement\n2\t\n3\tKenyon students researching study-abroad programs currently have to rely on outside sites that are poorly maintained and hard to search for specific answers (housing, meals, social life, academics). The Kenyon Center for Global Engagement (CGE) wants its own site where student Ambassadors who've actually attended a program write about it, but CGE must review every post before it goes public — nothing unapproved can reach a reader, and an Ambassador must never be able to touch anyone else's writing or the site's structure.\n4\t\n5\t## Solution\n6\t\n7\tA CMS with two roles — **Staff** (admin) and **Ambassador** (editor), see `CONTEXT.md` — where Ambassadors write and submit Posts, Staff review and publish them, and the public site is a static export organized as Home → Continent → Country → Program, with Posts grouped and filterable by Topic on their Program page. `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/ADR-003`, `ADR-004` are the settled vocabulary and decisions this spec builds on; `notes/future-work.md` lists what's deliberately deferred.\n8\t\n9\t## User Stories\n10\t\n11\t**Login (capability 1)**\n12\t1. As a Staff member, I want to log in with my email and password, so that I can access the admin console.\n13\t2. As an Ambassador, I want to log in with my email and password, so that I can write and manage my own posts.\n14\t3. As any user, I want a wrong password refused without the response revealing whether the account exists, so that no one can probe for valid emails.\n15\t4. As a deactivated user, I want my login refused, so that I can't access the system after my account is deactivated.\n16\t5. As any logged-in user, I want to log out, so that I can end my session on a shared computer.\n17\t\n18\t**Roles (capability 2)**\n19\t6. As a Staff member, I want every Ambassador capability available to me too, so that I can write and submit my own Posts without a second account.\n20\t7. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from any admin-only route, so that I can't reach user management or page authoring.\n21\t8. As an anonymous visitor, I want to be redirected to login when I request an admin route, so that the admin console stays private.\n22\t\n23\t**Posts: authoring and the review gate (capability 3, ADR-004)**\n24\t9. As an Ambassador, I want to create a new draft Post under a Program, so that I can start writing about my experience there.\n25\t10. As an Ambassador, I want to edit my own draft Post's title, body, and Topic, so that I can revise it before submitting.\n26\t11. As an Ambassador, I want to delete my own draft Post, after confirming \"are you sure?\", so that I don't lose it to a misclick but can still abandon it.\n27\t12. As an Ambassador, I want to submit my draft for review, so that CGE can decide whether to publish it.\n28\t13. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from editing or deleting my Post once it's pending or published, so that nothing changes mid-review or after it's live without CGE knowing.\n29\t14. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from touching another Ambassador's Post in any way, so that I can't edit, delete, or resubmit someone else's writing.\n30\t15. As a Staff member, I want to publish a pending Post, so that it goes live on the public site.\n31\t16. As a Staff member, I want to bounce a pending Post back to draft, so that its author can revise it before I reconsider.\n32\t17. As a Staff member, I want to publish my own draft Post directly, so that I don't have to route my own work through a review queue.\n33\t18. As a Staff member, I want the option to submit my own Post to pending instead, so that another Staff member can review it first.\n34\t19. As a Staff member, I want to edit or delete any Post regardless of status or author, so that I can fix a problem or remove content without waiting on anyone.\n35\t20. As a Staff member, I want to unpublish a live Post back to draft, so that I can pull it down for a larger rewrite.\n36\t\n37\t**Pages and the content tree (capability 4)**\n38\t21. As a Staff member, I want to create a Page nested under an existing Page (Home, a Continent, or a Country), so that I can build out the Continent → Country → Program tree.\n39\t22. As a Staff member, I want to create a standalone Page directly under Home (e.g. \"About CGE\"), so that I can publish information that isn't travel content.\n40\t23. As a Staff member, I want to flag a Page to show in the footer, so that standalone pages are reachable without cluttering the main navigation.\n41\t24. As a Staff member, I want to edit or delete any Page, so that I can keep the site's structure current as programs change.\n42\t25. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from creating, editing, or deleting any Page, so that the site's structure stays under CGE's control.\n43\t\n44\t**Topic (ADR-004 scope note, field notes)**\n45\t26. As a visitor reading a Program page, I want its Posts grouped by Topic, so that I can jump straight to Housing or Academics instead of scrolling through everything.\n46\t27. As a visitor reading a Program page, I want to filter to one Topic or see everything, so that I only see what I'm looking for.\n47\t28. As an Ambassador, I want to tag my Post with a Topic when I write it, so that it lands in the right section of the Program page.\n48\t\n49\t**Public navigation (field notes, client brief)**\n50\t29. As a visitor on any public page, I want a nav bar with Home and the Continents, so that I can jump to a different region from anywhere.\n51\t30. As a visitor drilled into a Program page, I want a breadcrumb trail (Home → Continent → Country → Program), so that I can see where I am and step back up a level at a time.\n52\t31. As a visitor, I want a footer linking to standalone pages like \"About CGE\" and \"Contact Us\", so that I can find that information from anywhere on the site.\n53\t32. As a visitor on a phone, I want the nav bar to wrap or collapse, so that it never runs off the screen.\n54\t\n55\t**Admin console (capability 5)**\n56\t33. As a Staff member, I want my admin home screen to be a live preview of the site, so that I land on what's actually published, the way WordPress's own admin works.\n57\t34. As a Staff member, I want a Dashboard tab with counts (Posts by status, Pages by level, active accounts), so that I can see the state of the whole site at a glance.\n58\t35. As a Staff member, I want a Pending queue tab listing every Post waiting on a decision, so that nothing sits unreviewed because no one thought to check.\n59\t36. As a Staff member, I want a Metrics tab showing Posts per Program, so that I can see which programs have no Ambassador content yet.\n60\t37. As an Ambassador, I want a \"My posts\" view listing my own drafts, pending, and published Posts, so that I can track what I've written without seeing anyone else's.\n61\t\n62\t**User management (capability 6)**\n63\t38. As a Staff member, I want an Accounts tab to create users, assign a role, and activate/deactivate an account, so that I can manage who has access.\n64\t39. As a Staff member, I want a deactivated user's draft Posts (and draft Pages, if they held the Staff role) deleted automatically, so that the content list doesn't fill up with abandoned half-finished work.\n65\t40. As a Staff member, I want a deactivated user's pending and published content left exactly as it is, so that I can still publish what's in the queue and readers keep seeing valuable published content.\n66\t41. As a visitor, I want a published Post to keep showing its original author's name even after that account is deactivated, so that the byline stays honest.\n67\t\n68\t**Public site and publish (capability 7)**\n69\t42. As a Staff member, I want `cms publish` to write only published Posts and Pages into `site/`, so that nothing in draft or pending ever leaks to the public.\n70\t43. As a Staff member, I want every link and asset in the exported HTML to be relative, so that the site works on its GitHub Pages subpath.\n71\t44. As a visitor, I want a Post's Markdown rendered as sanitized HTML, so that nothing an Ambassador wrote can inject a script into the page I'm reading.\n72\t45. As a Staff member, I want a slug frozen the instant something is published, so that a link a reader has already shared never breaks.\n73\t\n74\t## Implementation Decisions\n75\t\n\n... [51 lines truncated] ..."},"type":"attachment","uuid":"feb7b359-8dd0-4aa4-acbd-9b106710250d","timestamp":"2026-10-05T04:19:05.909Z","rendered":[{"content":"<system-reminder>\nNote: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-adam-leider-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-CMS-Project-IPHS-400/eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce/scratchpad/spec-body.md changed on disk since you last read it. As a visitor drilled into a Program page, I want a breadcrumb trail (Home → Continent → Country → Program), so that I can see where I am and step back up a level at a time.\n52\t31. As a visitor, I want a footer linking to standalone pages like \"About CGE\" and \"Contact Us\", so that I can find that information from anywhere on the site.\n53\t32. As a visitor on a phone, I want the nav bar to wrap or collapse, so that it never runs off the screen.\n54\t\n55\t**Admin console (capability 5)**\n56\t33. As a Staff member, I want my admin home screen to be a live preview of the site, so that I land on what's actually published, the way WordPress's own admin works.\n57\t34. As a Staff member, I want a Dashboard tab with counts (Posts by status, Pages by level, active accounts), so that I can see the state of the whole site at a glance.\n58\t35. As a Staff member, I want a Pending queue tab listing every Post waiting on a decision, so that nothing sits unreviewed because no one thought to check.\n59\t36. As a Staff member, I want a Metrics tab showing Posts per Program, so that I can see which programs have no Ambassador content yet.\n60\t37. As an Ambassador, I want a \"My posts\" view listing my own drafts, pending, and published Posts, so that I can track what I've written without seeing anyone else's.\n61\t\n62\t**User management (capability 6)**\n63\t38. As a Staff member, I want an Accounts tab to create users, assign a role, and activate/deactivate an account, so that I can manage who has access.\n64\t39. As a Staff member, I want a deactivated user's draft Posts (and draft Pages, if they held the Staff role) deleted automatically, so that the content list doesn't fill up with abandoned half-finished work.\n65\t40. As a Staff member, I want a deactivated user's pending and published content left exactly as it is, so that I can still publish what's in the queue and readers keep seeing valuable published content.\n66\t41. As a visitor, I want a published Post to keep showing its original author's name even after that account is deactivated, so that the byline stays honest.\n67\t\n68\t**Public site and publish (capability 7)**\n69\t42. As a Staff member, I want `cms publish` to write only published Posts and Pages into `site/`, so that nothing in draft or pending ever leaks to the public.\n70\t43. As a Staff member, I want every link and asset in the exported HTML to be relative, so that the site works on its GitHub Pages subpath.\n71\t44. As a visitor, I want a Post's Markdown rendered as sanitized HTML, so that nothing an Ambassador wrote can inject a script into the page I'm reading.\n72\t45. As a Staff member, I want a slug frozen the instant something is published, so that a link a reader has already shared never breaks.\n73\t\n74\t## Implementation Decisions\n75\t\n\n... {"parentUuid":"050b56fb-e05c-42e1-9fe9-aa0afe6a471f","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"1b88342b-69b6-469d-bd1f-186fcf52ff3c","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01UzxoWv2NA2jwedVhg6NAkA","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t## Problem Statement\n2\t\n3\tKenyon students researching study-abroad programs currently have to rely on outside sites that are poorly maintained and hard to search for specific answers (housing, meals, social life, academics). The Kenyon Center for Global Engagement (CGE) wants its own site where student Ambassadors who've actually attended a program write about it, but CGE must review every post before it goes public — nothing unapproved can reach a reader, and an Ambassador must never be able to touch anyone else's writing or the site's structure.\n4\t\n5\t## Solution\n6\t\n7\tA CMS with two roles — **Staff** (admin) and **Ambassador** (editor), see `CONTEXT.md` — where Ambassadors write and submit Posts, Staff review and publish them, and the public site is a static export organized as Home → Continent → Country → Program, with Posts grouped and filterable by Topic on their Program page. `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/ADR-003`, `ADR-004` are the settled vocabulary and decisions this spec builds on; `notes/future-work.md` lists what's deliberately deferred.\n8\t\n9\t## User Stories\n10\t\n11\t**Login (capability 1)**\n12\t1. As a Staff member, I want to log in with my email and password, so that I can access the admin console.\n13\t2. As an Ambassador, I want to log in with my email and password, so that I can write and manage my own posts.\n14\t3. As any user, I want a wrong password refused without the response revealing whether the account exists, so that no one can probe for valid emails.\n15\t4. As a deactivated user, I want my login refused, so that I can't access the system after my account is deactivated.\n16\t5. As any logged-in user, I want to log out, so that I can end my session on a shared computer.\n17\t\n18\t**Roles (capability 2)**\n19\t6. As a Staff member, I want every Ambassador capability available to me too, so that I can write and submit my own Posts without a second account.\n20\t7. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from any admin-only route, so that I can't reach user management or page authoring.\n21\t8. As an anonymous visitor, I want to be redirected to login when I request an admin route, so that the admin console stays private.\n22\t\n23\t**Posts: authoring and the review gate (capability 3, ADR-004)**\n24\t9. As an Ambassador, I want to create a new draft Post under a Program, so that I can start writing about my experience there.\n25\t10. As an Ambassador, I want to edit my own draft Post's title, body, and Topic, so that I can revise it before submitting.\n26\t11. As an Ambassador, I want to delete my own draft Post, after confirming \"are you sure?\", so that I don't lose it to a misclick but can still abandon it.\n27\t12. As an Ambassador, I want to submit my draft for review, so that CGE can decide whether to publish it.\n28\t13. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from editing or deleting my Post once it's pending or published, so that nothing changes mid-review or after it's live without CGE knowing.\n29\t14. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from touching another Ambassador's Post in any way, so that I can't edit, delete, or resubmit someone else's writing.\n30\t15. As a Staff member, I want to publish a pending Post, so that it goes live on the public site.\n31\t16. As a Staff member, I want to bounce a pending Post back to draft, so that its author can revise it before I reconsider.\n32\t17. As a Staff member, I want to publish my own draft Post directly, so that I don't have to route my own work through a review queue.\n33\t18. As a Staff member, I want the option to submit my own Post to pending instead, so that another Staff member can review it first.\n34\t19. As a Staff member, I want to edit or delete any Post regardless of status or author, so that I can fix a problem or remove content without waiting on anyone.\n35\t20. As a Staff member, I want to unpublish a live Post back to draft, so that I can pull it down for a larger rewrite.\n36\t\n37\t**Pages and the content tree (capability 4)**\n38\t21. As a Staff member, I want to create a Page nested under an existing Page (Home, a Continent, or a Country), so that I can build out the Continent → Country → Program tree.\n39\t22. As a Staff member, I want to create a standalone Page directly under Home (e.g. \"About CGE\"), so that I can publish information that isn't travel content.\n40\t23. As a Staff member, I want to flag a Page to show in the footer, so that standalone pages are reachable without cluttering the main navigation.\n41\t24. As a Staff member, I want to edit or delete any Page, so that I can keep the site's structure current as programs change.\n42\t25. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from creating, editing, or deleting any Page, so that the site's structure stays under CGE's control.\n43\t\n44\t**Topic (ADR-004 scope note, field notes)**\n45\t26. As a visitor reading a Program page, I want its Posts grouped by Topic, so that I can jump straight to Housing or Academics instead of scrolling through everything.\n46\t27. As a visitor reading a Program page, I want to filter to one Topic or see everything, so that I only see what I'm looking for.\n47\t28. As an Ambassador, I want to tag my Post with a Topic when I write it, so that it lands in the right section of the Program page.\n48\t\n49\t**Public navigation (field notes, client brief)**\n50\t29. As a visitor on any public page, I want a nav bar with Home and the Continents, so that I can jump to a different region from anywhere.\n51\t30. As a visitor drilled into a Program page, I want a breadcrumb trail (Home → Continent → Country → Program), so that I can see where I am and step back up a level at a time.\n52\t31. As a visitor, I want a footer linking to standalone pages like \"About CGE\" and \"Contact Us\", so that I can find that information from anywhere on the site.\n53\t32. As a visitor on a phone, I want the nav bar to wrap or collapse, so that it never runs off the screen.\n54\t\n55\t**Admin console (capability 5)**\n56\t33. As a Staff member, I want my admin home screen to be a live preview of the site, so that I land on what's actually published, the way WordPress's own admin works.\n57\t34. As a Staff member, I want a Dashboard tab with counts (Posts by status, Pages by level, active accounts), so that I can see the state of the whole site at a glance.\n58\t35. As a Staff member, I want a Pending queue tab listing every Post waiting on a decision, so that nothing sits unreviewed because no one thought to check.\n59\t36. As a Staff member, I want a Metrics tab showing Posts per Program, so that I can see which programs have no Ambassador content yet.\n60\t37. As an Ambassador, I want a \"My posts\" view listing my own drafts, pending, and published Posts, so that I can track what I've written without seeing anyone else's.\n61\t\n62\t**User management (capability 6)**\n63\t38. As a Staff member, I want an Accounts tab to create users, assign a role, and activate/deactivate an account, so that I can manage who has access.\n64\t39. As a Staff member, I want a deactivated user's draft Posts (and draft Pages, if they held the Staff role) deleted automatically, so that the content list doesn't fill up with abandoned half-finished work.\n65\t40. As a Staff member, I want a deactivated user's pending and published content left exactly as it is, so that I can still publish what's in the queue and readers keep seeing valuable published content.\n66\t41. As a visitor, I want a published Post to keep showing its original author's name even after that account is deactivated, so that the byline stays honest.\n67\t\n68\t**Public site and publish (capability 7)**\n69\t42. As a Staff member, I want `cms publish` to write only published Posts and Pages into `site/`, so that nothing in draft or pending ever leaks to the public.\n70\t43. As a Staff member, I want every link and asset in the exported HTML to be relative, so that the site works on its GitHub Pages subpath.\n71\t44. As a visitor, I want a Post's Markdown rendered as sanitized HTML, so that nothing an Ambassador wrote can inject a script into the page I'm reading.\n72\t45. As a Staff member, I want a slug frozen the instant something is published, so that a link a reader has already shared never breaks.\n73\t\n74\t## Implementation Decisions\n75\t\n76\t**Module split** (new, per this spec): `app/models.py` — plain SQLite access (no ORM, per ADR-002), `User`/`Page`/`Post` reads and writes. `app/services/` — pure rules with no FastAPI or SQLite dependency: slug generation, the status state machine, the deactivation cascade. `app/routes/` — thin HTTP handlers that call services for decisions and models for persistence. `templates/` — unchanged, `admin/` and `public/` subtrees as already established.\n77\t\n78\t**Data model** (logical, fields not file-bound):\n79\t- `User`: id, email, password_hash (argon2), role (`admin`/`editor`), display_name, active (bool), timestamps.\n80\t- `Page`: id, parent_id (nullable only for Home), title, slug, body (Markdown), status (`draft`/`published` — **no `pending`**: only Staff author Pages, and Staff can self-publish, so there's never a reviewer to wait on), `show_in_footer` (bool), author_id, timestamps, published_at.\n81\t- `Post`: id, program_id (must reference a Program-level Page), title, slug, body (Markdown), topic (`general`/`housing`/`meals`/`social-life`/`academics`/`other`), status (`draft`/`pending`/`published`), author_id, timestamps, published_at.\n82\t\n83\t**Status state machine** (services layer; a decision this precise is clearer as a table than prose):\n84\t\n85\t| From | Action | Who | To |\n86\t|---|---|---|---|\n87\t| draft | submit | the Post's own author (any role) | pending |\n88\t| pending | publish | any admin | published |\n89\t| pending | bounce | any admin | draft |\n90\t| draft | self-publish | admin, **own Post only** | published |\n91\t| published | unpublish | any admin | draft |\n92\t\n93\tNo other transition exists. In particular, an admin cannot move *someone else's* draft straight to published — it must be submitted to pending first, same as anyone's. This keeps \"an Ambassador's post is never published without someone deciding to put it through pending\" true even when the decider is an admin, not just an Ambassador.\n94\t\n95\t**Content edit/delete permission** (orthogonal to status, from `CONTEXT.md`'s Staff/Ambassador entries): admin — any Post or Page, any status, always. Editor — only their own Post, only while draft. Never any Page.\n96\t\n97\t**Slug generation**: derived from title (lowercase, non-alphanumeric runs collapsed to hyphens). Regenerates on every title change while status is draft; frozen the moment status leaves draft, even if an admin edits the title afterward. On a collision with a sibling under the same parent, append `-2`, `-3`, … — not grilled explicitly; flagged below.\n98\t\n99\t**Deactivation cascade** (services layer): on deactivating any user (Staff or Ambassador), delete their draft Posts and, if they held the Staff role, their draft Pages. Leave pending and published content untouched, byline intact. The grill settled this for Ambassadors specifically (A11); extending it uniformly to a deactivated Staff account is a synthesis decision, flagged below.\n100\t\n101\t**Public URL / nav contract**: a Page's public path is the slug chain of its ancestors from Home (Home = site root); a Post's path nests under its Program's path. A footer-flagged standalone Page still gets a path under Home, just excluded from Home's own child listing (`CONTEXT.md`, Page).\n102\t\n103\t**Admin console layout**: Staff's landing screen is a live preview of the site inside the console; sidebar tabs are Dashboard, Pending queue, Accounts, Page hierarchy, Metrics. Ambassador's sidebar is just \"My posts\". No reviewer assignment and no notifications on the pending queue — any admin can act on any pending Post.\n104\t\n105\t## Testing Decisions\n106\t\n107\tA good test asserts externally observable behavior — status code, redirect target, response HTML, a written file's contents, or a service function's return value/raised error — never an internal implementation detail.\n108\t\n109\t- **HTTP seam** (`TestClient`, prior art: `tests/test_t00.py`, `conftest.py`'s `client_as(role)`): login success/failure/deactivated, every admin-only route rejected for an editor and for an anonymous request, Post/Page CRUD and every status-transition route end-to-end, CSRF rejection on a POST with the token stripped, the Dashboard/Pending-queue/Accounts/Metrics/My-posts screens, nav bar/breadcrumb/footer HTML on public pages.\n110\t- **`render_site()` seam** (prior art: `test_publish_writes_a_site`, `test_published_html_uses_relative_paths`): a draft or pending Post/Page present but absent from the output, every href/src relative, sanitized Markdown in the exported HTML, a frozen slug surviving a post-publish title edit, nav/breadcrumb/footer present in the static files.\n111\t- **Services seam** (new, no HTTP or DB — plain pytest functions): every cell of the status state-machine table including the disallowed combinations (e.g. editor attempting publish, admin attempting draft→published on someone else's Post), slug generation and its collision suffixing, the deactivation cascade's decision of which Posts/Pages to delete vs. keep.\n112\t\n113\t## Out of Scope\n114\t\n115\tPer ADR-003: private messaging, a visitor/commenter account role, an IT/developer role, view/comment-based search filters, in-CMS suggested-edit tooling. Per `notes/future-work.md`: trash/restore with a 30-day auto-delete (plain delete only, with a confirmation prompt), scheduled/visibility-gated publish. Per the grill (A6): sitewide/scoped search is a stretch ticket after the 7 capabilities, client-side against a JSON index built at publish time — not part of this spec's core tickets.\n116\t\n117\t## Further Notes\n118\t\n119\tFour points in this spec were synthesized (not explicitly grilled) because they follow directly from decisions already settled — flagging them here so they can be corrected before `/to-tickets` cuts this into tickets:\n120\t\n121\t1. **Pages have no `pending` status** — only `draft`/`published`, since only Staff author Pages and Staff can self-publish (ADR-004 only ever discusses Posts).\n122\t2. **Slug collisions** get a numeric suffix (`-2`, `-3`, …), scoped to siblings sharing a parent — never explicitly asked.\n123\t3. **The deactivation cascade applies to a deactivated Staff account too**, not only Ambassadors (A11 was framed around graduating Ambassadors specifically).\n124\t4. **An admin can't draft→published someone else's Post** — only their own; everyone else's still needs pending. ADR-004's \"into or out of published\" language is satisfied by the unpublish transition (published→draft), not by a second direct-publish shortcut.\n125\t\n126\t`scripts/seed_demo.py` will need Asia/Africa/Europe as Continents, a couple Countries under each, one or two Programs per Country, and generated placeholder copy at every level (A1) — a tickets-stage task, noted here so it isn't lost.\n127\t"}]},"uuid":"a626411b-074f-4b7d-b4b4-d8bc1be0a063","timestamp":"2026-10-05T04:23:00.943Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/tmp/claude-1000/-home-adam-leider-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-CMS-Project-IPHS-400/eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce/scratchpad/spec-body.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nKenyon students researching study-abroad programs currently have to rely on outside sites that are poorly maintained and hard to search for specific answers (housing, meals, social life, academics). The Kenyon Center for Global Engagement (CGE) wants its own site where student Ambassadors who've actually attended a program write about it, but CGE must review every post before it goes public — nothing unapproved can reach a reader, and an Ambassador must never be able to touch anyone else's writing or the site's structure.\n\n## Solution\n\nA CMS with two roles — **Staff** (admin) and **Ambassador** (editor), see `CONTEXT.md` — where Ambassadors write and submit Posts, Staff review and publish them, and the public site is a static export organized as Home → Continent → Country → Program, with Posts grouped and filterable by Topic on their Program page. `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/ADR-003`, `ADR-004` are the settled vocabulary and decisions this spec builds on; `notes/future-work.md` lists what's deliberately deferred.\n\n## User Stories\n\n**Login (capability 1)**\n1. As a Staff member, I want to log in with my email and password, so that I can access the admin console.\n2. As an Ambassador, I want to log in with my email and password, so that I can write and manage my own posts.\n3. As any user, I want a wrong password refused without the response revealing whether the account exists, so that no one can probe for valid emails.\n4. As a deactivated user, I want my login refused, so that I can't access the system after my account is deactivated.\n5. As any logged-in user, I want to log out, so that I can end my session on a shared computer.\n\n**Roles (capability 2)**\n6. As a Staff member, I want every Ambassador capability available to me too, so that I can write and submit my own Posts without a second account.\n7. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from any admin-only route, so that I can't reach user management or page authoring.\n8. As an anonymous visitor, I want to be redirected to login when I request an admin route, so that the admin console stays private.\n\n**Posts: authoring and the review gate (capability 3, ADR-004)**\n9. As an Ambassador, I want to create a new draft Post under a Program, so that I can start writing about my experience there.\n10. As an Ambassador, I want to edit my own draft Post's title, body, and Topic, so that I can revise it before submitting.\n11. As an Ambassador, I want to delete my own draft Post, after confirming \"are you sure?\", so that I don't lose it to a misclick but can still abandon it.\n12. As an Ambassador, I want to submit my draft for review, so that CGE can decide whether to publish it.\n13. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from editing or deleting my Post once it's pending or published, so that nothing changes mid-review or after it's live without CGE knowing.\n14. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from touching another Ambassador's Post in any way, so that I can't edit, delete, or resubmit someone else's writing.\n15. As a Staff member, I want to publish a pending Post, so that it goes live on the public site.\n16. As a Staff member, I want to bounce a pending Post back to draft, so that its author can revise it before I reconsider.\n17. As a Staff member, I want to publish my own draft Post directly, so that I don't have to route my own work through a review queue.\n18. As a Staff member, I want the option to submit my own Post to pending instead, so that another Staff member can review it first.\n19. As a Staff member, I want to edit or delete any Post regardless of status or author, so that I can fix a problem or remove content without waiting on anyone.\n20. As a Staff member, I want to unpublish a live Post back to draft, so that I can pull it down for a larger rewrite.\n\n**Pages and the content tree (capability 4)**\n21. As a Staff member, I want to create a Page nested under an existing Page (Home, a Continent, or a Country), so that I can build out the Continent → Country → Program tree.\n22. As a Staff member, I want to create a standalone Page directly under Home (e.g. \"About CGE\"), so that I can publish information that isn't travel content.\n23. As a Staff member, I want to flag a Page to show in the footer, so that standalone pages are reachable without cluttering the main navigation.\n24. As a Staff member, I want to edit or delete any Page, so that I can keep the site's structure current as programs change.\n25. As an Ambassador, I want to be blocked from creating, editing, or deleting any Page, so that the site's structure stays under CGE's control.\n\n**Topic (ADR-004 scope note, field notes)**\n26. As a visitor reading a Program page, I want its Posts grouped by Topic, so that I can jump straight to Housing or Academics instead of scrolling through everything.\n27. As a visitor reading a Program page, I want to filter to one Topic or see everything, so that I only see what I'm looking for.\n28. As an Ambassador, I want to tag my Post with a Topic when I write it, so that it lands in the right section of the Program page.\n\n**Public navigation (field notes, client brief)**\n29. As a visitor on any public page, I want a nav bar with Home and the Continents, so that I can jump to a different region from anywhere.\n30. As a visitor drilled into a Program page, I want a breadcrumb trail (Home → Continent → Country → Program), so that I can see where I am and step back up a level at a time.\n31. As a visitor, I want a footer linking to standalone pages like \"About CGE\" and \"Contact Us\", so that I can find that information from anywhere on the site.\n32. As a visitor on a phone, I want the nav bar to wrap or collapse, so that it never runs off the screen.\n\n**Admin console (capability 5)**\n33. As a Staff member, I want my admin home screen to be a live preview of the site, so that I land on what's actually published, the way WordPress's own admin works.\n34. As a Staff member, I want a Dashboard tab with counts (Posts by status, Pages by level, active accounts), so that I can see the state of the whole site at a glance.\n35. As a Staff member, I want a Pending queue tab listing every Post waiting on a decision, so that nothing sits unreviewed because no one thought to check.\n36. As a Staff member, I want a Metrics tab showing Posts per Program, so that I can see which programs have no Ambassador content yet.\n37. As an Ambassador, I want a \"My posts\" view listing my own drafts, pending, and published Posts, so that I can track what I've written without seeing anyone else's.\n\n**User management (capability 6)**\n38. As a Staff member, I want an Accounts tab to create users, assign a role, and activate/deactivate an account, so that I can manage who has access.\n39. As a Staff member, I want a deactivated user's draft Posts (and draft Pages, if they held the Staff role) deleted automatically, so that the content list doesn't fill up with abandoned half-finished work.\n40. As a Staff member, I want a deactivated user's pending and published content left exactly as it is, so that I can still publish what's in the queue and readers keep seeing valuable published content.\n41. As a visitor, I want a published Post to keep showing its original author's name even after that account is deactivated, so that the byline stays honest.\n\n**Public site and publish (capability 7)**\n42. As a Staff member, I want `cms publish` to write only published Posts and Pages into `site/`, so that nothing in draft or pending ever leaks to the public.\n43. As a Staff member, I want every link and asset in the exported HTML to be relative, so that the site works on its GitHub Pages subpath.\n44. As a visitor, I want a Post's Markdown rendered as sanitized HTML, so that nothing an Ambassador wrote can inject a script into the page I'm reading.\n45. As a Staff member, I want a slug frozen the instant something is published, so that a link a reader has already shared never breaks.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n**Module split** (new, per this spec): `app/models.py` — plain SQLite access (no ORM, per ADR-002), `User`/`Page`/`Post` reads and writes. `app/services/` — pure rules with no FastAPI or SQLite dependency: slug generation, the status state machine, the deactivation cascade. `app/routes/` — thin HTTP handlers that call services for decisions and models for persistence. `templates/` — unchanged, `admin/` and `public/` subtrees as already established.\n\n**Data model** (logical, fields not file-bound):\n- `User`: id, email, password_hash (argon2), role (`admin`/`editor`), display_name, active (bool), timestamps.\n- `Page`: id, parent_id (nullable only for Home), title, slug, body (Markdown), status (`draft`/`published` — **no `pending`**: only Staff author Pages, and Staff can self-publish, so there's never a reviewer to wait on), `show_in_footer` (bool), author_id, timestamps, published_at.\n- `Post`: id, program_id (must reference a Program-level Page), title, slug, body (Markdown), topic (`general`/`housing`/`meals`/`social-life`/`academics`/`other`), status (`draft`/`pending`/`published`), author_id, timestamps, published_at.\n\n**Status state machine** (services layer; a decision this precise is clearer as a table than prose):\n\n| From | Action | Who | To |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| draft | submit | the Post's own author (any role) | pending |\n| pending | publish | any admin | published |\n| pending | bounce | any admin | draft |\n| draft | self-publish | admin, **own Post only** | published |\n| published | unpublish | any admin | draft |\n\nNo other transition exists. In particular, an admin cannot move *someone else's* draft straight to published — it must be submitted to pending first, same as anyone's. This keeps \"an Ambassador's post is never published without someone deciding to put it through pending\" true even when the decider is an admin, not just an Ambassador.\n\n**Content edit/delete permission** (orthogonal to status, from `CONTEXT.md`'s Staff/Ambassador entries): admin — any Post or Page, any status, always. Editor — only their own Post, only while draft. Never any Page.\n\n**Slug generation**: derived from title (lowercase, non-alphanumeric runs collapsed to hyphens). Regenerates on every title change while status is draft; frozen the moment status leaves draft, even if an admin edits the title afterward. On a collision with a sibling under the same parent, append `-2`, `-3`, … — not grilled explicitly; flagged below.\n\n**Deactivation cascade** (services layer): on deactivating any user (Staff or Ambassador), delete their draft Posts and, if they held the Staff role, their draft Pages. Leave pending and published content untouched, byline intact. The grill settled this for Ambassadors specifically (A11); extending it uniformly to a deactivated Staff account is a synthesis decision, flagged below.\n\n**Public URL / nav contract**: a Page's public path is the slug chain of its ancestors from Home (Home = site root); a Post's path nests under its Program's path. A footer-flagged standalone Page still gets a path under Home, just excluded from Home's own child listing (`CONTEXT.md`, Page).\n\n**Admin console layout**: Staff's landing screen is a live preview of the site inside the console; sidebar tabs are Dashboard, Pending queue, Accounts, Page hierarchy, Metrics. Ambassador's sidebar is just \"My posts\". No reviewer assignment and no notifications on the pending queue — any admin can act on any pending Post.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\nA good test asserts externally observable behavior — status code, redirect target, response HTML, a written file's contents, or a service function's return value/raised error — never an internal implementation detail.\n\n- **HTTP seam** (`TestClient`, prior art: `tests/test_t00.py`, `conftest.py`'s `client_as(role)`): login success/failure/deactivated, every admin-only route rejected for an editor and for an anonymous request, Post/Page CRUD and every status-transition route end-to-end, CSRF rejection on a POST with the token stripped, the Dashboard/Pending-queue/Accounts/Metrics/My-posts screens, nav bar/breadcrumb/footer HTML on public pages.\n- **`render_site()` seam** (prior art: `test_publish_writes_a_site`, `test_published_html_uses_relative_paths`): a draft or pending Post/Page present but absent from the output, every href/src relative, sanitized Markdown in the exported HTML, a frozen slug surviving a post-publish title edit, nav/breadcrumb/footer present in the static files.\n- **Services seam** (new, no HTTP or DB — plain pytest functions): every cell of the status state-machine table including the disallowed combinations (e.g. editor attempting publish, admin attempting draft→published on someone else's Post), slug generation and its collision suffixing, the deactivation cascade's decision of which Posts/Pages to delete vs. keep.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nPer ADR-003: private messaging, a visitor/commenter account role, an IT/developer role, view/comment-based search filters, in-CMS suggested-edit tooling. Per `notes/future-work.md`: trash/restore with a 30-day auto-delete (plain delete only, with a confirmation prompt), scheduled/visibility-gated publish. Per the grill (A6): sitewide/scoped search is a stretch ticket after the 7 capabilities, client-side against a JSON index built at publish time — not part of this spec's core tickets.\n\n## Further Notes\n\nFour points in this spec were synthesized (not explicitly grilled) because they follow directly from decisions already settled — flagging them here so they can be corrected before `/to-tickets` cuts this into tickets:\n\n1. **Pages have no `pending` status** — only `draft`/`published`, since only Staff author Pages and Staff can self-publish (ADR-004 only ever discusses Posts).\n2. **Slug collisions** get a numeric suffix (`-2`, `-3`, …), scoped to siblings sharing a parent — never explicitly asked.\n3. **The deactivation cascade applies to a deactivated Staff account too**, not only Ambassadors (A11 was framed around graduating Ambassadors specifically).\n4. **An admin can't draft→published someone else's Post** — only their own; everyone else's still needs pending. ADR-004's \"into or out of published\" language is satisfied by the unpublish transition (published→draft), not by a second direct-publish shortcut.\n\n`scripts/seed_demo.py` will need Asia/Africa/Europe as Continents, a couple Countries under each, one or two Programs per Country, and generated placeholder copy at every level (A1) — a tickets-stage task, noted here so it isn't lost.\n","numLines":127,"startLine":1,"totalLines":127}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"050b56fb-e05c-42e1-9fe9-aa0afe6a471f","session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

As a Staff member, I want an Accounts tab to create users, assign a role, and activate/deactivate an account, so that I can manage who has access.\n39. As a Staff member, I want a deactivated Ambassador's draft Posts deleted automatically, so that the content list doesn't fill up with abandoned half-finished student work.\n39a. As a Staff member, I want a deactivated Staff colleague's drafts left in place, editable and publishable by any other Staff member, so that CGE's own unfinished work isn't lost just because whoever started it left.\n40. As a Staff member, I want a deactivated user's pending and published content left exactly as it is, so that I can still publish what's in the queue and readers keep seeing valuable published content.\n41. As a visitor, I want a published Post to keep showing its original author's name even after that account is deactivated, so that the byline stays honest.\n\n**Public site and publish (capability 7)**\n42. As a Staff member, I want `cms publish` to write only published Posts and Pages into `site/`, so that nothing in draft or pending ever leaks to the public.\n43. As a Staff member, I want every link and asset in the exported HTML to be relative, so that the site works on its GitHub Pages subpath.\n44. As a visitor, I want a Post's Markdown rendered as sanitized HTML, so that nothing an Ambassador wrote can inject a script into the page I'm reading.\n45. As a visitor, I want a Post's Markdown rendered as sanitized HTML, so that nothing an Ambassador wrote can inject a script into the page I'm reading.\n45. If the author's\naccount is later deactivated, what happens to a draft depends on their role:\nan Ambassador's draft is deleted (nothing worth keeping from a student who's\nleft, and it would otherwise clutter the content list); a Staff member's\ndraft is left exactly as it is — it's usually CGE's own ongoing work, not a\ndeparting student's, and any other Staff member can already view, edit,\npublish, or delete it like any other Post. Either way, a pending Post is\nleft alone, since Staff still need to act on it, and a published Post is\nleft alone too and keeps its byline, since its value to readers has nothing\nto do with whether its author's account is still active.","originalFile":"# Kenyon CGE Study Abroad CMS\n\nGlossary for the CMS built for the Kenyon Center for Global Engagement's study\nabroad blog. Client: `notes/client-brief.md`. The 7 fixed capabilities this\nvocabulary has to satisfy: `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` §3.3.\n\n## Language\n\n**Page**:\nSite content with a parent — except Home, which has none. Most Pages sit in\nthe Continent → Country → Program tree below Home, but a Page can also stand\nalone under Home directly, like About CGE or Contact Us. Home's own body\nlists the Continents, full stop — standalone Pages under Home don't appear\nthere. Every other Page's body lists its non-footer child Pages, if it has\nany, and its own Posts grouped by Topic, if it has any — no separate\ntemplate per level otherwise. A reader finds a Page three ways: the top nav\nbar (Home plus the Continents, always, regardless of what else exists), a\nbreadcrumb trail built from its parent chain (e.g. Home → Asia → Japan →\nKenyon-in-Kyoto), and the footer, which lists any Page with its \"show in\nfooter\" flag checked — a standalone Page under Home is only reachable this\nway, so it's expected to always have that flag checked. Staff add more\nContinents, Countries, Programs, and standalone Pages later through the\nnormal page editor, the same way the seed set was created.\n_Avoid_: continent page, country page, program page as if they were distinct\ntypes — they are all just Pages at different places in the tree. Also avoid\nassuming every Page is travel content — About CGE and Contact Us are Pages\ntoo, just standalone ones under Home.\n\n**Continent**:\nA Page one level below Home — Asia, Africa, and Europe in the seed data. Lists\nits child Country Pages.\n\n**Country**:\nA Page one level below a Continent. Lists its child Program Pages.\n\n**Program**:\nA Page one level below a Country — the level Posts are written under. Lists\nits own Posts, grouped by Topic, with a filter by Topic.\n\n**Post**:\nA dated blog entry written under a Program Page: title, slug, Markdown body,\nTopic, author, timestamps, and a status of draft, pending, or published.\n_Avoid_: entry, article.\n\n**Slug**:\nThe URL-safe name derived from a Post's or Page's title. Nobody edits it by\nhand — it regenerates automatically whenever the title changes while the\ncontent is still draft, then freezes the moment it's published, so a shared\nlink never breaks. Shown read-only wherever the content is edited.\n_Avoid_: implying it's a form field a Staff or Ambassador fills in — it has\nno input of its own, only a display.\n\n**Topic**:\nThe category a Post is tagged with, used to group and filter Posts on their\nProgram page like forum sections (read-only — no replies or discussion):\nGeneral, Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics, or Other.\n_Avoid_: treating General as a different kind of thing from the rest — see\nHot Topic for how the two relate.\n\n**Hot Topic**:\nAny Topic value other than General — Housing, Meals, Social Life, Academics,\nor Other. The brief and field notes' informal name for that subset; there is\nno separate field for it, only Topic.\n_Avoid_: treating Hot Topic as a type distinct from Topic, or as a field of\nits own — see Topic.\n\n**Status** (of a Post):\ndraft → pending → published. *Draft*: the author is still writing; only they\ncan edit it, and it is not public. *Pending*: the author has submitted it for\nreview and can no longer edit it; it is still not public — anyone with the\nadmin role can act on it, not just a specific reviewer, and there is no\nnotification when a Post lands in the queue. *Published*: live on the public\nsite. Only an admin can move a Post into or out of published, and only an\nadmin can bounce pending back to draft. One shortcut: an admin can publish\ntheir own draft directly, skipping pending, since there is no one else to\nreview it against; an admin's draft can also go through pending like anyone\nelse's if they want another admin's eyes on it first. The shortcut applies\nonly to an admin's own Post — an admin cannot push someone else's draft\nstraight to published without it passing through pending. If the author's\naccount is later deactivated: a draft is deleted (nothing worth keeping from\nsomeone who's left, and it would otherwise clutter the content list); a\npending Post is left alone, since Staff still need to act on it; a published\nPost is left alone too and keeps its byline, since its value to readers has\nnothing to do with whether its author's account is still active.\n_Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list\nnames only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit\nsubmit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004).\n\n**Role**:\nTwo roles, per the manual: *admin*, shown in the UI as **Staff**, and *editor*,\nshown in the UI as **Ambassador**. The mapping is strict and permission-based,\nnot title-based — admin/editor stay the internal/code names (the manual's own\nvocabulary); Staff/Ambassador are what the site and this glossary call them.\nStaff have every capability Ambassadors have (they can write and submit Posts\ntoo) plus admin-only capabilities (publish, user management).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\" / \"student ambassador\" in place of Staff/Ambassador once\ninside the CMS's own vocabulary — those are brief language, not the product's.\n\n**Staff**:\nThe UI-facing name for the admin role (see Role). Can manage users; create,\nedit, delete, and publish any Page or Post; and do everything an Ambassador\ncan, including writing and submitting their own Posts — with the option to\neither self-publish a draft directly or submit it to pending like anyone\nelse (see Status).\n_Avoid_: \"CGE staff\", admin — see Role.\n\n**Ambassador**:\nThe UI-facing name for the editor role (see Role): a student who writes and\nsubmits their own Posts. Can create, edit, and delete only their own Posts,\nand only while draft (see Status); cannot touch another user's Post, cannot\ncreate or edit a Page, and cannot publish.\n_Avoid_: \"student ambassador\", editor — see Role.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":77,"oldLines":11,"newStart":77,"newLines":15,"lines":[" else's if they want another admin's eyes on it first. The shortcut applies"," only to an admin's own Post — an admin cannot push someone else's draft"," straight to published without it passing through pending. If the author's","-account is later deactivated: a draft is deleted (nothing worth keeping from","-someone who's left, and it would otherwise clutter the content list); a","-pending Post is left alone, since Staff still need to act on it; a published","-Post is left alone too and keeps its byline, since its value to readers has","-nothing to do with whether its author's account is still active.","+account is later deactivated, what happens to a draft depends on their role:","+an Ambassador's draft is deleted (nothing worth keeping from a student who's","+left, and it would otherwise clutter the content list); a Staff member's","+draft is left exactly as it is — it's usually CGE's own ongoing work, not a","+departing student's, and any other Staff member can already view, edit,","+publish, or delete it like any other Post. Either way, a pending Post is","+left alone, since Staff still need to act on it, and a published Post is","+left alone too and keeps its byline, since its value to readers has nothing","+to do with whether its author's account is still active."," _Avoid_: treating pending as a synonym for draft — the manual's capability list"," names only draft/published, but this project adds pending as the explicit"," submit-for-review step the client asked for (see ADR-004)."]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"55c0944f-e74f-43bf-9ead-e334b20da8da","session_id":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/CMS-Project-IPHS-400","sessionId":"eb860014-76cc-4c1a-a94b-31f3cba54bce","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"leider1-ui/CMS-Project-IPHS-400"}

{"parentUuid":"6d740932-630c-49dd-961e-bb6de7776a2c","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"34ba61a4-779b-445c-9caf-5bcf1e2eb48e","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01H4Q26xLBQazkUYqqR27eug","type":"tool_result","content":"---\nname: to-tickets\ndescription: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker (edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker).\ndisable-model-invocation: true\n---\n\n# To Tickets\n\nBreak a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets**: tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.\n\nThe issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Gather context\n\nWork from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.\n\n### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)\n\nIf you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\nLook for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. \"Make the change easy, then make the easy change.\"\n\n### 3. Draft vertical slices\n\nBreak the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.\n\n<vertical-slice-rules>\n\n- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests): vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer\n- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own\n- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window\n- Any prefactoring should be done first\n\n</vertical-slice-rules>\n\nGive each ticket its **blocking edges**: the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.\n\n**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change (rename a column, retype a shared symbol) whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket; green is promised only there.\n\n### 4. Quiz the user\n\nPresent the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:\n\n- **Title**: short descriptive name\n- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first\n- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work\n\nAsk the user:\n\n- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)\n- Are the blocking edges correct: does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?\n- Should any tickets be merged or split further?\n\nIterate until the user approves the breakdown.\n\n### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker\n\nPublish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured; the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:\n\n- **Local files** → write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first). Each file's \"Blocked by\" lists the numbers/titles it depends on. Use the per-ticket file template below: one ticket per file, never a single combined file.\n- **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking / sub-issue relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's \"Blocked by\" to the blocking issues. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise; the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.\n\nWork the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.\n\nDo NOT close or modify any parent issue.\n\n<local-ticket-template>\n\n# <NN>: <Ticket title>\n\n**What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not a layer-by-layer implementation list.\n\n**Blocked by:** the numbers/titles of the tickets that gate this one, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n**Status:** ready-for-agent\n\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 1\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 2\n\n</local-ticket-template>\n\n<issue-template>\n\n## Parent\n\nA reference to the parent issue on the tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).\n\n## What to build\n\nThe end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not layer-by-layer implementation.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Criterion 1\n- [ ] Criterion 2\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- A reference to each blocking ticket, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n</issue-template>\n\nIn either form, avoid specific file paths or code snippets: they go stale fast. Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Parent\\n\\nPart of the spec, #1.\\n\\n## What to build\\n\\nStaff builds the Continent → Country → Program tree (or a standalone Page under Home) from the admin console; a published Page is live both in the admin console's preview and through `cms publish`, with the Home+Continents nav bar, a breadcrumb trail, and the footer for flagged pages — so the public site is genuinely deployable this early, before Posts exist.\\n\\n## Acceptance criteria\\n\\n- [ ] Staff creates, edits, and deletes a Page nested under any existing Page, or standalone under Home with \\\"show in footer\\\" checked.\\n- [ ] Deleting a Page asks \\\"are you sure?\\\" before it runs.\\n- [ ] A Page's slug auto-generates from its title, regenerates while draft, and freezes the moment it's published.\\n- [ ] An Ambassador is blocked from every Page-authoring route (403), and an anonymous request is redirected to login.\\n- [ ] `cms publish` writes every published Page to `site/`: the nav bar (Home + Continents), a breadcrumb trail built from the parent chain, the footer for flagged pages, and each Page's body listing its non-footer children (Home's body lists only the Continents) — every link relative.\\n- [ ] A draft Page never appears in `cms publish`'s output.\\n- [ ] The nav bar wraps or collapses at phone width.\\n- [ ] `scripts/seed_demo.py` seeds Asia, Africa, and Europe as Continents, a couple of Countries under each, one or two Programs per Country, plus an About CGE and a Contact Us standalone page (footer-flagged) — all with generated placeholder copy, published.\\n\\n## Blocked by\\n\\n- #2 (T01: Login, sessions, and role-gated from the sidebar they reach a Dashboard, a filterable content list, the Pending queue, the Page hierarchy, and Metrics.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Logging in as Staff lands on a live preview of the published site inside the console.\n- [ ] A sidebar reaches: Dashboard, Content list, Pending queue, Page hierarchy, Metrics.\n- [ ] Dashboard shows counts: Posts by status, Pages by level, active accounts.\n- [ ] The content list shows every Post and Page together, filterable by status (draft/pending/published) and by type (Post/Page).\n- [ ] The Pending queue lists every pending Post (title, author, submitted date) with a link straight into its editor; no reviewer assignment, no notifications.\n- [ ] Metrics shows Posts per Program, so a Program with zero Posts is visible at a glance.\n- [ ] An Ambassador is blocked from every route in this ticket.\n- [ ] \\`scripts/seed_demo.py\\`'s existing seed data (Pages, Posts in all three statuses, accounts) is enough to make every count and list non-empty on a fresh clone.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #$num2 (T02: Pages — the content tree, authoring, and early cms publish)\n- #$num4 (T04: Posts — the review-gate state machine)\nEOF\nnum7=$(gh issue create --title \"T07: Staff console — dashboard, content list, pending queue, page hierarchy, metrics\" --label \"ticket\" --body-file \"$SCRATCH/tickets/07.md\" | grep -oE '[0-9]+$')\necho \"T07 -> #$num7\"; #2 ===\n## Parent\n\nPart of the spec, #1.\n\n## What to build\n\nStaff and Ambassador can log in with email + password; a wrong password is refused without revealing whether the account exists; a deactivated account can't log in; any logged-in user can log out; CSRF protection is wired for every state-changing form from here on; a reusable login-required / admin-required gate exists, proven against one stub protected route.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] A seeded Staff (admin) and Ambassador (editor) user can each log in with their email/password and reach a logged-in page.\n- [ ] A wrong password is refused with the same generic message whether or not the email exists.\n- [ ] A seeded deactivated user cannot log in, with the same generic failure message.\n- [ ] Logout ends the session; a previously-reachable logged-in page is no longer reachable afterward.\n- [ ] Every state-changing (POST) route rejects a request whose CSRF token is missing or wrong.\n- [ ] A stub admin-only route rejects an Ambassador (403) and an anonymous request (redirect to login), and allows a Staff member.\n- [ ] `scripts/seed_demo.py` seeds one admin (Staff), one editor (Ambassador), and one deactivated user, passwords from `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`/`CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD`/env.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- None (can start immediately).\n\n\n=== #3 ===\n## Parent\n\nPart of the spec, #1.\n\n## What to build\n\nStaff builds the Continent → Country → Program tree (or a standalone Page under Home) from the admin console; a published Page is live both in the admin console's preview and through `cms publish`, with the Home+Continents nav bar, a breadcrumb trail, and the footer for flagged pages — so the public site is genuinely deployable this early, before Posts exist.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Staff creates, edits, and deletes a Page nested under any existing Page, or standalone under Home with \"show in footer\" checked.\n- [ ] Deleting a Page asks \"are you sure?\" before it runs.\n- [ ] A Page's slug auto-generates from its title, regenerates while draft, and freezes the moment it's published.\n- [ ] An Ambassador is blocked from every Page-authoring route (403), and an anonymous request is redirected to login.\n- [ ] `cms publish` writes every published Page to `site/`: the nav bar (Home + Continents), a breadcrumb trail built from the parent chain, the footer for flagged pages, and each Page's body listing its non-footer children (Home's body lists only the Continents) — every link relative.\n- [ ] A draft Page never appears in `cms publish`'s output.\n- [ ] The nav bar wraps or collapses at phone width.\n- [ ] `scripts/seed_demo.py` seeds Asia, Africa, and Europe as Continents, a couple of Countries under each, one or two Programs per Country, plus an About CGE and a Contact Us standalone page (footer-flagged) — all with generated placeholder copy, published.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #2 (T01: Login, sessions, and role-gated access)\n\n\n=== #4 ===\n## Parent\n\nPart of the spec, #1.\n\n## What to build\n\nAn Ambassador writes a draft Post under a Program — title, Markdown body, Topic — and sees a sanitized preview of how it will render before doing anything else with it; a Staff member can do the same to any Post while it's draft.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An Ambassador creates, edits, and deletes their own draft Post (title, body, Topic) under a Program.\n- [ ] Deleting a draft Post asks \"are you sure?\" before it runs.\n- [ ] The editor shows a sanitized-HTML preview of the current Markdown body — an injected `<script>` or `onerror=` attribute never shows up live in the preview.\n- [ ] A Post's slug auto-generates from its title and regenerates while draft.\n- [ ] An Ambassador is blocked from creating, editing, or deleting another user's Post.\n- [ ] A Staff member can create, edit, and delete any draft Post, same as an Ambassador can their own.\n- [ ] `scripts/seed_demo.py` seeds a few draft Posts across different Topics under the seeded Programs, authored by the seeded editor.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #3 (T02: Pages — the content tree, authoring, and early cms publish)\n\n\n=== #5 ===\n## Parent\n\nPart of the spec, #1.\n\n## What to build\n\nThe full draft → pending → published flow from ADR-004: an Ambassador submits their draft; a Staff member publishes or bounces a pending Post, publishes their own draft directly, or unpublishes a live Post; every disallowed transition is rejected.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An Ambassador submits their own draft Post, moving it to pending; they can no longer edit or delete it afterward.\n- [ ] Any Staff member can publish or bounce (back to draft) a pending Post, regardless of who wrote it.\n- [ ] A Staff member can publish their own draft Post directly, or submit it to pending like anyone else, at their choice.\n- [ ] A Staff member can unpublish a published Post back to draft.\n- [ ] An admin cannot move someone else's draft straight to published without it passing through pending first.\n- [ ] An Ambassador attempting any transition other than submitting their own draft is rejected.\n- [ ] Every cell of the state-machine table, including every disallowed combination, is covered by a services-seam unit test with no HTTP or DB involved.\n- [ ] `scripts/seed_demo.py` seeds Posts in each of the three statuses (draft, pending, published) so the workflow is visible on a fresh clone.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #4 (T03: Posts — draft authoring, Topic, and a Markdown preview)\n\n\n=== #6 ===\n## Parent\n\nPart of the spec, #1.\n\n## What to build\n\nPublished Posts reach the public site, grouped and filterable by Topic on their Program page; `cms publish`'s output (started in T02 for Pages) now includes Posts too.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] A published Program page lists its Posts grouped by Topic.\n- [ ] A visitor can filter a Program page to one Topic, or see all Posts.\n- [ ] A Post's Markdown body is sanitized before it is rendered anywhere, public or admin.\n- [ ] A draft or pending Post never appears in a public response or in `cms publish`'s output.\n- [ ] `cms publish` writes every published Post under its Program's path, with every link relative.\n- [ ] A Post's slug stays frozen through a title edit made after it is published.\n- [ ] `scripts/seed_demo.py`'s published Posts (seeded in T04) render correctly end-to-end through `cms publish`.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #5 (T04: Posts — the review-gate state machine)\n\n\n=== #7 ===\n## Parent\n\nPart of the spec, #1.\n\n## What to build\n\nStaff manages accounts from an Accounts tab — create, assign role, activate/deactivate — and deactivating a user triggers the role-specific cascade from `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] A Staff member creates a user, assigns them a role (Staff or Ambassador), and can deactivate or reactivate them.\n- [ ] Deactivating an Ambassador deletes their draft Posts.\n- [ ] Deactivating a Staff member leaves their drafts untouched, and any other Staff member can view, edit, publish, or delete them like any other content.\n- [ ] A deactivated user's pending and published Posts are left exactly as they are.\n- [ ] A published Post keeps its original author's byline after that account is deactivated.\n- [ ] An Ambassador is blocked from every Accounts route.\n- [ ] `scripts/seed_demo.py` seeds one already-deactivated Ambassador with a leftover draft (to show it's gone) and one already-deactivated Staff member with a leftover draft (to show it's kept).\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #2 (T01: Login, sessions, and role-gated access)\n- #5 (T04: Posts — the review-gate state machine)\n\n\n=== #8 ===\n## Parent\n\nPart of the spec, #1.\n\n## What to build\n\nStaff's landing screen is a live preview of the published site; from the sidebar they reach a Dashboard, a filterable content list, the Pending queue, the Page hierarchy, and Metrics.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Logging in as Staff lands on a live preview of the published site inside the console.\n- [ ] A sidebar reaches: Dashboard, Content list, Pending queue, Page hierarchy, Metrics.\n- [ ] Dashboard shows counts: Posts by status, Pages by level, active accounts.\n- [ ] The content list shows every Post and Page together, filterable by status (draft/pending/published) and by type (Post/Page).\n- [ ] The Pending queue lists every pending Post (title, author, submitted date) with a link straight into its editor; no reviewer assignment, no notifications.\n- [ ] Metrics shows Posts per Program, so a Program with zero Posts is visible at a glance.\n- [ ] An Ambassador is blocked from every route in this ticket.\n- [ ] `scripts/seed_demo.py`'s existing seed data (Pages, Posts in all three statuses, accounts) is enough to make every count and list non-empty on a fresh clone.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #3 (T02: Pages — the content tree, authoring, and early cms publish)\n- #5 (T04: Posts — the review-gate state machine)\n\n\n=== #9 ===\n## Parent\n\nPart of the spec, #1.\n\n## What to build\n\nAn Ambassador's sidebar shows a single \"My posts\" view listing their own Posts, split by status, and nothing belonging to anyone else.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An Ambassador's sidebar shows only \"My posts\" (and logout).\n- [ ] \"My posts\" lists their own drafts, pending, and published Posts, grouped or clearly labeled by status.\n- [ ] No other user's Post appears anywhere in this view.\n- [ ] An Ambassador cannot reach any Staff-console route (Dashboard, Accounts, Page hierarchy, Metrics, Pending queue) from here or directly.\n- [ ] `scripts/seed_demo.py`'s seeded editor has at least one Post in each status so \"My posts\" has something in every section on a fresh clone.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #5 (T04: Posts — the review-gate state machine)\n\n\n=== #10 ===\n## Parent\n\nPart of the spec, #1.\n\n## What to build\n\nClient-side search, scoped to the page it is launched from — a Continent page searches only its own Countries/Programs/Posts, a Country page only its own, a Program page only its own Posts — against a JSON index built at `cms publish` time.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `cms publish` writes a JSON search index alongside `site/`'s HTML.\n- [ ] A search box on a Continent/Country/Program page returns only results scoped to that page's own subtree.\n- [ ] Results support a date filter and a relevance ordering.\n- [ ] No server-side component is introduced; the index is static and the search runs entirely in the browser.\n- [ ] Explicitly a stretch ticket (spec A6): deferred until after T01–T08 if time doesn't allow.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #6 (T05: Public
